## 2. How to run it

Everything is already installed and configured. Node is managed by nvm.

```bash
# interactive terminals pick this up from ~/.zshrc automatically.
# a non-interactive shell (like an agent's Bash tool) does NOT, so prefix with:
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . /opt/homebrew/opt/nvm/nvm.sh; nvm use 22
export COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0
```

Toolchain: Node 22.23.2 (nvm), Yarn 3.2.1 (via corepack), Docker 28.4.0, gh 2.100.0 (authed as angrapsas).
Do NOT use Node 24 — some suites fail on it. Homebrew also has a Node 26 that nvm shadows.

### Two separate apps

**A. The monorepo** at `~/medusa` — the actual Medusa source, what we make PRs against.

```bash
cd ~/medusa
yarn install                                    # ~1 min
yarn build                                      # ~2.5 min, 80 packages
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev          # admin dashboard dev server on :5173
yarn workspace @medusajs/ui storybook           # design system on :6006
```

**B. A scaffolded store** at `~/my-store` — created with create-medusa-app, used to click around a
real running store. Uses PUBLISHED medusa packages from npm, NOT the local source, so changes to
`~/medusa` do NOT show up here.

```bash
docker start medusa-postgres                    # postgres:15 on :5433, db `my_store`, postgres/postgres
cd ~/my-store/apps/backend && npm run dev       # admin at :9000/app
```

Admin login exists (created during Sprint 0). Store is seeded: 4 products, 20 variants, 2 orders,
1 region (Europe/EUR), 1 sales channel.

**Which one to use:** :5173 to see your own dashboard changes. :9000 to see a fully working store
with data. They are different codebases.

**Running my local code end to end (used for the Lightning Talk screenshots, Oct 19):**
```bash
git -C ~/medusa stash apply stash@{0}     # vite globals fix, otherwise :5173 is blank. Revert after.
cd ~/medusa/integration-tests/http
export DB_HOST=localhost:5433 DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD=postgres DB_TEMP_NAME=medusa_manual NODE_ENV=development
../../node_modules/.bin/medusa db:migrate       # once; finishes but may not exit, Ctrl+C after "Links sync completed"
../../node_modules/.bin/medusa user -e admin@test.com -p supersecret   # once
PORT=9001 ADMIN_CORS=http://localhost:5174 AUTH_CORS=http://localhost:5174 ../../node_modules/.bin/medusa start   # ~5-10 min to boot
cd ~/medusa && VITE_MEDUSA_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:9001 yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev --port 5174
```
The `medusa_manual` database on medusa-postgres already exists (admin user, a "European Warehouse"
location). Sample CSVs are in `~/csci535-notes/screenshots/csv-samples/`. The integration-tests
config disables the built-in admin, so :9001/app does not exist; use :5174.

### Tests

```bash
cd ~/medusa
yarn workspace @medusajs/medusa test            # Jest, backend, 13 suites / 95 tests
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test         # Vitest, frontend, ~13 files / 93 tests
yarn turbo run test --no-daemon --no-cache --force --continue   # everything; KEEP --continue
```

Frameworks: **Jest 29** (backend), **Vitest 3** + @testing-library/react + jsdom (frontend).
No Playwright, no Cypress, no browser automation anywhere. ~1050 `.spec.ts(x)` files.

Integration tests need their own containers and will take the my-store DB offline:

```bash
docker stop medusa-postgres
docker run -d --name medusa-pg -e POSTGRES_USER=postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -p 5433:5432 postgres:16-alpine
docker run -d --name medusa-redis -p 6380:6379 redis:7-alpine
cd ~/medusa && DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD=postgres \
  yarn workspace @medusajs/region test:integration      # 18/18
# teardown
docker rm -f medusa-pg medusa-redis && docker start medusa-postgres
```

## 3. Known broken things (all upstream Medusa, not our fork)

Our fork only adds STUDENTS.md and course files on top of Medusa 2.17.2. These are real upstream bugs.

**1. 467 unit tests fail on a clean checkout.** `@medusajs/icons` 464/464 and `@medusajs/ui` 3/40.
All from one cause: `packages/design-system/icons/package.json` declares
`react: "^18.3.1 || ^19.0.0"` in devDependencies, so Yarn nests react@19.2.6 inside that package
while `react-dom@18.3.1` stays hoisted at root. React 19 elements + React 18 renderer =
"Objects are not valid as a React child". Fix: scoped resolution `"@medusajs/icons/react": "^18.3.1"`
in root package.json — precedent already exists there for `@redocly/cli/react`.
**68 of 70 packages pass.** Confirmed by three of us independently. NOT your machine.

**2. The standalone dashboard dev server renders a blank page.**
`packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts` defines only 3 of the 6 globals the source needs.
Missing: `__AUTH_TYPE__`, `__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__`, `__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__`.
`src/lib/client/client.ts:3` throws a ReferenceError before React mounts. The bundled admin at
:9000 works because `admin-bundler/src/utils/config.ts:52-57` defines all six. Config was last
touched 2024-10-09; the source added those globals in late 2025. Nobody has fixed it.
Workaround already in the repo: `vi.hoisted()` in three spec files sets the globals for tests.

**3. Form validation errors never display anywhere in the dashboard.**
`@hookform/resolvers@3.4.2` with `zod@4.2.0`. Resolvers v3 doesn't understand zod 4 errors, so
instead of putting them in form state it throws. **116 files use zodResolver, 104 render
`<Form.ErrorMessage />`, and none of them can show anything.** Submitting an invalid form just
silently refuses. Verified by running validation directly: errors exist with messages, they just
never reach the form.

My issues (all written by teammates, all merged, all on the Sprint 2 milestone):
- **#41** (medium) Promotion CSV import. PR **#84**. Same design as #40/#11: validate every row

  (his AI log) with the rubric.
- D6 UML diagrams for #58: PR **#88**, `docs/sprint2/diagrams/58-angrapsas{-class,-sequence}.png`
  plus the Q&A `.md`. Sources and simplified quiz versions in `~/csci535-notes/diagrams/`.
- D5 logs PR **#94** (`ai-logs/sprint2/angrapsas/`). AI Assistance comments on #41, #58, #63, PR #89.
- D7 check-in PR **#74**. Team report PR **#95**. Tag **v2.17.2-csci435-s2**.

**#58 in one paragraph (I get asked about this):** completing a cart when an item sold out returned
a 400 with no cart, so the storefront could not show which item was the problem. The error comes
from `ensureInventoryLevels` in the inventory module, thrown as `NOT_ALLOWED`. The promotion-limit
and subscription errors from the same workflow are also `NOT_ALLOWED`, so the route could not branch
on type. I attached the existing `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY` code to the error at its source and added
a `statusOKErrorCodes` list to `packages/medusa/src/api/store/carts/[id]/complete/route.ts`.
Rejected alternatives: allow the whole `NOT_ALLOWED` type (swallows the other two), pre-check stock
(extra query on every checkout and still racy), new error type (the HTTP error handler does not know
it, so other routes 500). Cost: handled errors now live in two lists, and the code appears in other
routes' error bodies, which required updating two reservation tests.

## 7. Showcase 2: Ponytail (Nov 8-10)

The team's second tech showcase was **Ponytail** (https://ponytail.dev,
github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail, MIT), a Claude Code plugin that injects a decision ladder
(stdlib → native platform feature → reuse existing project code → only then write new code) so the
agent stops over-engineering. Published benchmarks: 54% less code, 27% faster, 20% lower API cost,
with validation and security never simplified away. Commands: `/ponytail-review` (scan the current
diff), `/ponytail-audit` (whole repo), `/ponytail-debt` (log deferred shortcuts).

## 9. Lessons learned

Medusa core is deliberately minimal; the plugin ecosystem fills feature gaps. **Before proposing
anything, search externally, not just the repo.** Ideas that looked like gaps but already exist as
official or community plugins: Shopify migration (Medusa's own MCP server does it), sales analytics
dashboard (Agilo and rsc-labs plugins), abandoned cart recovery (community plugin + Medusa guide).

The proposals that survive are ones a plugin **cannot** add — engine behavior, admin API routes,
core defaults. That's why #16 and #23 hold up.

Also verified as genuinely missing: order CSV import (products have import+export, orders have
export only), customer export, and **a count of how many times a product has sold** —
`order_line_item` has indexed `product_id` and `variant_id` plus `quantity`, so the data is there
and indexed; nobody surfaced it. That last one is a natural sequel to #9 (order count + lifetime
spend for customers, which lefecko already merged).

From Sprint 1:
- **Read the code before trusting an issue's scope.** #32 already existed, #16 was smaller than written.
- **Claim issues and get spec review comments at the start of the sprint.** Sprint 1 all landed on the last day.
- **Never paste issue/PR text copied from the terminal.** It mangled #32 and #40 twice. Save to a file and
  post with `gh issue edit N --body-file <file>` / `gh pr create --body-file <file>`.
- **Run parallel work in separate git worktrees**: `git worktree add ~/medusa-<n> -b <branch> origin/develop`.
- **Watch AI scope creep.** On #11 it added a whole-number rule for weights nobody asked for. Tell it to stick to
  the acceptance criteria and check commit messages before every commit.

From Sprint 2:
- **Sprint 0 lost D4/D5 points because no issue comment linked the logs.** The link has to open the
  log file itself, not the folder. One "AI Assistance" comment per contributor per issue.
- **The error you are looking for is often not where the obvious code is.** On #58 I assumed
  `confirm-inventory.ts` because it already used `INSUFFICIENT_INVENTORY`. That step does not run on
  cart completion at all. Trace the real path before designing.
- **Tag an error at its source, match on the tag at the boundary.** Beats pattern-matching messages
  or widening a type list that other errors share.
- **Every PR needs the Tech Debt section**, split into Introduced (a tradeoff you chose) and
  Encountered (pre-existing, scoped out). Sprint 3 adds Test Evidence on top of it.
- **Reviews must be substantive.** On #89 I checked out the branch, ran it, and reverted the author's
  fix to confirm his new test actually failed. That is the kind of thing worth writing down in the
  review.
- **Diagrams need a legend and annotations or they lose points**, even when the structure is right.

## 11. Conventions to follow

- Prettier: no semicolons, double quotes, 2-space indent, ES5 trailing commas. `npx prettier --check <files>`
- Files kebab-case, types PascalCase, functions camelCase, constants SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, DB fields snake_case
- Commit style is mixed on the team: conventional (`feat(dashboard): ...`) and plain imperative both appear
- **Changesets required** — add one as a separate `chore:` commit. See `.changeset/` for format
- PR description format: What / Why / How / Testing, in plain prose, first person. Include the
  command to run the tests. No checklists, no bolded headers — teammates don't use them
- `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailers appear on some commits (lefecko uses them, upstream Medusa
  does too). Not required
- AI logs go to `ai-logs/sprint<N>/<username>/YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from
  the issue or PR it documents, as a full URL that opens the file itself, not the folder
- My commits: short plain subject only ("Add ...", "Fix ..."), no body, no Co-Authored-By line
- Every PR gets a teammate review with the course rubric. **Never self-approve or self-merge**

**New in Sprint 3 (see `sprint3.md` for the full text):**
- Every PR description needs a **Test Evidence** table (one row per AC: test, level, source of the
  expected value) on top of the Tech Debt section. The source of an expected value may never be
  "what the code currently returns"
- A PR merges only after a teammate approves **the latest commit**. Pushing after an approval
  invalidates it
- A **spec review comment on the issue, before coding**, that states what the reviewer checked
- Use `Closes #<issue>` in the PR description and attach issues and PRs to the sprint milestone
- D6 mutation testing uses **StrykerJS** (Jest runner for backend packages, Vitest runner for the
  dashboard), run only on the files the PR changed, with before/after JSON reports committed

## 12. How I like to work

- Find the code myself first, then use AI to check my understanding. The course grades this
  ("concept location") and I have to be able to explain every line of my own PRs
- Verify claims by running things, don't assert from reading. Prove a test fails without the fix
- Don't post to GitHub (issues, PRs, comments, reviews, tags) without showing me the exact text first
- Keep writing plain. No em dashes, no AI-sounding scaffolding. Match my teammates' register

## Things that must improve from Sprint 2

1. **Open PRs early.** In Sprint 2 most PRs were opened in the last two days, leaving no time for
   review. Sprint 3 needs a code PR by the mid-sprint check-in (D7).

2. **Independent approval before merging.** A PR is merged only after a teammate approves **its
   latest commit**. Merging without an approval, or after pushing new commits since the approval,
   is not allowed. Once approved, the author may merge. Request the review on GitHub and notify the
   reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond (approve or request changes) within 24 hours.

3. **Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked.** Before coding starts, a teammate
   posts a review comment **on the issue itself**. The comment states what the reviewer checked:
   whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and
   whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If there are problems, the reviewer lists
   them and the author updates the spec. "Looks good!" with nothing about what was checked is not
   acceptable.

4. **Link PRs and issues.** Every code PR links the issue it addresses. Use `Closes #<issue>` in the
   PR description. Attach issues and code PRs to the Sprint 3 milestone.

5. **AI logs must be real logs.** Prompts and the AI's output (SpecStory recommended). Not accepted:
   summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share link to a chat, or tool output without the
   prompts that produced it. File names: `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log from the
   issue or PR it documents.

6. **The sprint report must render.** Check tables and links display correctly on GitHub (no escaped
   `\|` or `\[`). Use the Sprint 3 sections, not a copy of a previous report.

## Deliverables

### D1 - Sprint Backlog (10 pts, team)

Same process as Sprint 2, including the priority on carryovers: unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into
the Sprint 3 backlog first, or you document on the issue why they are dropped.

**Scope minimums (same as Sprint 2):**

| Role | Minimum |
|---|---|
| Each CSCI 435 member | at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points) |
| **Each CSCI 535 (grad) member** | **at least 2 medium issues + 1 additional small issue** |

**Scope must be justified.** Each issue states its scope (small or medium) and one or two sentences
on why: which components it touches and how much change is expected. The instructor or TA may
reclassify an issue whose scope is clearly overstated.

**Hardening issues (optional).** One of your issues may be a hardening issue: work that makes the
existing system more reliable rather than adding a feature. Good sources:
- The baseline run (D8): failing tests, flaky tests, broken CI checks on the default branch
- Tech debt recorded in the "Introduced" and "Encountered" fields of Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs
- Known bugs found in reviews, after merging, or by teammates
- The upstream issue tracker, for bugs in the parts of the system the team works on

A hardening issue is scoped like any other issue and **must include evidence that the problem is
fixed**:
- **Bug fix:** a test that fails before the fix and passes after
- **Flaky test:** the root cause, plus enough repeated runs before and after to show the change
  (for example 20 runs for a unit test, 10 for an E2E test)
- **Broken or missing CI check:** links to CI runs before and after
- **Failing tests in the baseline:** pass/fail counts before and after, and the cause of each group

Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without fixing its cause counts as
**small at most**.

**Team feature.** When posted, split it into sub-issues, each with its own owner, spec (D2) and
scope. Link each sub-issue to the feature issue. Sub-issues count toward the scope minimum. Add the
sub-issues to the Sprint 3 milestone and adjust the backlog.

Create a Sprint 3 milestone in GitHub and attach all selected issues.

**What to provide in D8:** link to the Sprint 3 milestone and the rationale for backlog decisions.

### D2 - Requirements Specification (20 pts, individual)

Same format and requirements as Sprint 1. Specs must be **written and reviewed before coding
begins**; see item 3 above for what counts as a review.

Hardening issues use a **bug format** (observed behavior, expected behavior, steps to reproduce,
other details) when they fix a defect. Otherwise a short **task format**: the problem, the goal,
acceptance criteria, other necessary details.

### D3 - Design Decisions (5 pts, individual)

Same as Sprint 2: each decision names **at least two concrete alternatives** and explains the choice.

### D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests (20 pts, individual)

Same workflow as Sprint 2, **including the Tech Debt section**. Sprint 3 adds a **Test Evidence**
section to every PR description. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description, so
you don't write it twice.

```markdown
## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: ... | ... | ... | ... |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** [...]

**AI-written tests:** [Which tests were written or modified by AI, and how you
checked that their expected values are correct. If none, write "None."]
```

**How to fill it in:**
- One row per acceptance criterion from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For
  PRs that change no product behavior (for example CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
- **Test(s):** the test name (and file, if not obvious). If checked manually, write `Manual:`
  followed by the steps and what you saw. If an AC is tested both ways, list both in the same row.
- **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E`, or `manual`.
- **Source of expected value:** where the expected result comes from. One of: `AC`,
  `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). **The current output of
  your own code is not a valid source**; a test whose expected value was copied from what the code
  returns cannot detect that the code is wrong.
- **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually only.
- You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for checking that it is accurate.

**Example:**

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: An end date before the start date is rejected with an error | `outOfOffice.schema.test.ts > rejects end before start` | unit | AC |
| AC2: The away badge appears on the booking page during the out-of-office window | `booking-ooo.e2e.ts > shows away badge in window` | E2E | AC |
| AC3: The badge text is readable in dark mode | Manual: enabled dark mode, opened the booking page during the window, badge text is readable | manual | issue discussion |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC3 depends on visual contrast, which our test setup does not check.

**If your fork has no CI that runs your tests** (ours does not run on PRs), include the command(s)
you ran and a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).

**Reviewers add one line to the code review rubric** (from Sprint 1 D4):

| Criterion | Score (1-10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Test evidence - does every AC have a test? Are the expected values justified? Which tests did you run locally? | | |

### D5 - AI Logs (5 pts, individual)

Same requirements as Sprint 1 and the AI Log Instructions, with the enforcement in item 5 above.

**Log storage:** `ai-logs/sprint3/angrapsas/`

### D6 - Mutation Testing (15 pts, individual) - NEW

**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (**mutants**), such as
flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test
fails, the mutant is **killed**. If all tests pass, the mutant **survived**: your tests did not
notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

**What to do.** For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests
(**CSCI 535: two such issues**; your small issue may be one of them):

1. Run a mutation testing tool **on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue**. Do not
   run it on the whole project.
2. Using the tool's report, **analyze every surviving mutant**: is it **equivalent** (it behaves
   exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a **gap** in your
   tests? If there are more than 10 survivors, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines
   your PR added or changed.
3. **Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant** that revealed a gap.
   Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent),
   say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the questions in the template.

**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (**StrykerJS: add `"json"` to
`reporters`**). Commit the report from the first run and the re-run as
`docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`. The mutation
scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in
the "after" report.

**A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.**

| Stack | Tool |
|---|---|
| **TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)** | **StrykerJS with the Jest runner** |
| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

**Note for us:** Medusa is mixed. Backend packages use **Jest**, the dashboard uses **Vitest**.
Pick the runner that matches the files the PR changed.

**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services,
choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits
the configuration used. **You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to)**, as long as you
run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

**Common problems to watch for:**
- **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any
  selected test fails, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where the baseline
  run helps). *Relevant to us: see HANDOFF section 3 and issue #98.*
- **Tests run against built code.** If tests run against compiled output (a `dist` folder) instead
  of the source, mutants in the source are never seen. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing,
  or choose tests that run on source. *Relevant to us: the integration tests load `dist`.*
- **Tests need services.** Some suites need a database or another service running. Start them first.
- **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run, make sure the tests that cover the mutated
  files are included. Otherwise mutants some test would catch are reported as survived or not
  covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
- **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by the PR keeps run time manageable.

**If you are blocked:** ask teammates first, someone may have a working setup. Still stuck, tell the
TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and the AI log of what you tried. The TA may approve
running the tool on a different issue or part of the code. **Problems reported at the end of the
sprint will not excuse a missing D6.**

**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-angrapsas.md`, using this template:

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>

**PR(s):** #...
**Tool:** ...
**Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]
**Command:** `...`
**Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%

## Surviving mutants

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [link] · Test: [file > test name] · Kills: [mutant location]

## Questions

1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the
   requirements? Explain.
3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and
   what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."
```

**Rubric:**

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| Tool run on the files changed by the PR; configuration, command, results and reports committed | 4 |
| Surviving mutants analyzed correctly (equivalent vs test gap, with explanation) | 4 |
| At least one new or strengthened test kills a surviving mutant; re-run confirms it | 4 |
| Answers to the questions show understanding, not just description | 3 |

**CSCI 535: the D6 score is the average of the two submissions.**

Also: **mutation testing** links to each member's D6 file; **hardening issues** and where they came

## Grading

100 points, 12% of the course grade. D1, D8 and D9 are team; everything else individual.

| Deliverable | Points | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| D1 Sprint Backlog | 10 | Team. Issues selected, scoped with justification, assigned, milestone created; carryover decisions documented |
| D2 Requirements Specification | 20 | Individual. User story format, INVEST, AC quality; **spec review on the issue before coding, showing what was checked** |
| D3 Design Decisions | 5 | Individual. At least one non-trivial decision per issue, with alternatives |
| D4 Pull Requests | 20 | Individual. See detail below |
| D5 AI Logs | 5 | Individual. Real logs, correctly named, linked from the issue or PR |
| D6 Mutation Testing | 15 | Individual. See rubric above |
| D7 Mid-Sprint Check-in | 5 | Individual. On time, substantive, PR linked = 5; late, thin, or no PR = 3; missing = 0 |
| D8 Sprint Report | 10 | Team. Completeness, specificity, quality of evidence; suite health section |
| D9 Sprint Release | 2 | Team. Tag convention; created after the last merge; description summarizes changes |
| D10 Reflection Survey | 8 | Individual. Required for completion |

### D4 PR grading detail

Aggregate across all PRs, normalized to 20 points.

| Criterion | Points per PR |
|---|---|
| Change correctly implements the acceptance criteria from D2 | 6 |
| Tests written or updated appropriately; **Test Evidence section complete**, every AC covered, expected values justified | 6 |
| PR description explains what changed and why; **Tech Debt section** present; issue linked | 3 |
| CI passes (or manual verification documented) | 3 |
| Code reviewed using the rubric (including the test evidence line); reviewer comment posted; **PR merged only after an approval on the latest commit** | 2 |

### Minimum bar

A team with no merged PRs (D4), no sprint report (D8), or no release (D9) receives a **0** for
Sprint 3 regardless of other deliverables.

### Extra credit

- A PR submitted to the **real upstream project** and accepted or under active review: up to **3
  bonus points per PR**, at the instructor's discretion.
- A **bug report filed upstream** that comes from your own testing work and is confirmed by the
  maintainers (by the time Sprint 4 is graded): up to **2 bonus points per report**.

*Note: our Sprint 1 and 2 work produced several real upstream findings (the icons React 19 version
conflict, the dashboard vite config missing globals, zodResolver v3 with zod 4 breaking all form
validation). Those are documented in HANDOFF section 3 and are genuine upstream bugs. Filing one
with evidence from our testing is free points.*

===== ISSUE 97 =====
Export promotions to CSV

## User Story
As a store admin, I want to export promotions to a CSV file in the same format the promotion import reads, so that I can review them in a spreadsheet, keep a backup, or copy them to another store.

## User Scenario
Maria is setting up a second store for a new region and wants the same 30 promotions. On the first store's Promotions page, she filters to Active promotions and clicks "Export." A message tells her the export is being prepared. A minute later a notification gives her a download link. She opens the file in a spreadsheet, changes a few discount values, and uses the existing "Import" button on the new store's Promotions page. All 30 promotions are created with their rules.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The promotions list has an "Export" action next to "Import."
2. The export includes every promotion matching the list's current filters and search, not only the current page.
3. The file uses the same column headers, in the same order, as the import template: Code, Type, Status, Automatic, Tax Inclusive, Usage Limit, Campaign ID, Discount Type, Discount Value, Currency Code, Target, Allocation, Max Quantity, Buy Min Quantity, Apply To Quantity, Rules, Target Rules, Buy Rules. Each promotion is one row.
4. Rules, Target Rules and Buy Rules use the import's format: `attribute:operator:value`, with multiple values joined by `|` and multiple rules joined by `;` (for example `currency_code:eq:eur;customer_group_id:in:cg_1|cg_2`).
5. Empty fields are written as empty cells, and booleans as `true`/`false`, as the import expects.
6. Round trip: importing an exported file (after removing or renaming conflicting codes) recreates promotions with the same settings and rules. A test checks this by parsing the export with the existing import parser (`import-promotions.ts`).
7. The export runs in the background, like the customer and product exports. `POST /admin/promotions/export` returns `202` with a `transaction_id`, and the admin gets a notification with a download link when the file is ready.
8. Tests: unit tests for converting a promotion to a CSV row (including rule formatting and the round trip), an HTTP integration test for the route and its filters, and a dashboard test for the Export action.

## Scope
**Medium.** It follows the existing customer export, which changed about 19 files: an admin route, a core-flows workflow and step that build the CSV in the background and send a notification, a JS SDK method and response type, and an Export action with translations on the promotions list. The new code is the conversion from a promotion and its rules to the import's CSV format, which needs unit, round-trip, HTTP integration and dashboard tests.

## Out of Scope
- Usage counts, campaign details and campaign budgets.
- Choosing which columns to export.
- Scheduled or automatic exports.
- Updating existing promotions by code on import. Import still only creates promotions.

## Open Questions
- Campaign ID: a campaign ID from one store means nothing in another. Should the export leave it blank, or keep it so a re-import into the same store links the campaign again?
- What should happen to a promotion with a rule the import can't read back? Skip it with a warning, export it anyway, or fail the export?
- Should the export always use the import's format, even if a promotion has fields that format doesn't cover?

--- COMMENTS ---

===== ISSUE 100 =====
Hold stock for shoppers during checkout

## User Story

As a store owner, I want stock held for a shopper while they check out so that customers don't lose items at the last step and the store doesn't oversell.

## User Scenario

Two shoppers want the last pair of shoes. The first one starts checkout, and the store holds the pair for a few minutes. The second shopper can't buy it during that time. The first shopper pays, and the order is placed.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft, incomplete)

- When a shopper starts checkout, stock for the items in the cart is held for a set time.
- Held stock is not available to other shoppers.
- When the order is placed, the hold becomes the order's reservation.
- If an item doesn't have enough stock when checkout starts, nothing is held and the shopper sees which items are unavailable.
- More criteria needed, based on the open questions below.

Acceptance criteria should also cover invalid input, failures, conflicts, and permissions, not only the main path.

## Out of Scope

- Holding stock when an item is added to the cart
- Emails or notifications about holds

## Open Questions

- What exactly counts as "starting checkout"?
- What happens when a hold expires while the shopper is still paying, or after the payment succeeds?
- What if the shopper changes the cart during checkout?
- What happens when two shoppers try to hold the last unit at the same moment?
- Which items are held? What about items that allow backorders, or stock in several locations?
- How do store admins see and control holds?
- What happens if expired holds are released late?
- What happens to existing data and installations after upgrading?

## Notes

Today, stock is reserved only when the cart is completed. Areas this touches: inventory, the checkout and cart completion flow, scheduled jobs, the store and admin APIs, and the admin UI.

## Design

To be filled in before implementation.

===== ISSUE 98 =====
Fix the failing test suites

## User Story
As a developer on this team, I want every test suite to pass in CI and in the dev container, so that a failing test means my change broke something rather than a known problem.

## User Scenario
Logan finishes a feature and runs the test suites before opening a PR. Today, 6 unrelated problems make several suites fail even on a clean `develop`: an HTTP types check, hundreds of icon tests, a database test that can't connect in the dev container, two flaky tests, and integration workers that run out of memory. He has to compare against `develop` by hand to find out whether any failure is his. Sometimes a flaky failure also stops other tests from running, including tests for his own feature. After this change, every suite passes on `develop` in both places. A failure on his branch points to his change.

## Background
All suites were run on `develop` in the dev container. The 6 problems:

| # | Problem | Tests affected | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Validate HTTP Types finds 10 mismatches between HTTP types and the API's validators. 9 are from upstream (product options, notifications). 1 came from our #42 analytics work: `AdminGetSalesSummaryParams` declares `start_date`/`end_date` as `string`, but the validator produces `Date`. | Validate HTTP Types CI job | CI and locally |
| 2 | `packages/design-system/icons` installs React 19.2.6 as a dev dependency (`"^18.3.1 \|\| ^19.0.0"`), but tests render with the repo's React 18.3.1. Every icon test throws "Objects are not valid as a React child." | 464 icons and 3 ui unit tests | Locally (the lockfile, so likely CI too) |
| 3 | `replace-zod-imports.test.ts` in `@medusajs/cli` changes the working directory to a temp folder and scans it. It's flaky: it failed 1 of 4 runs. | 2 unit tests | Random |
| 4 | The utils test database helper (`packages/core/utils/src/dal/mikro-orm/integration-tests/__fixtures__/database.ts`) builds its URL without `DB_PORT`, so it always connects on 5432. The dev container's Postgres is on 5433. | 32 tests in `mikro-orm-repository.spec.ts` | Dev container |
| 5 | The Redis engine's `race.spec.ts` › "should manage saving multiple async steps in concurrency" can hit its 20s timeout under load. It passed 3 of 3 reruns alone. The package's `test:integration` script chains its 4 spec files with `&&`, so a failure here stops `retry-interval.spec.ts` and `failed-execution-retention.spec.ts` (the #66/#67 tests) from running. | 1 test + 2 files after it | Random, under load |
| 6 | In the module and HTTP integration suites, a Jest worker's memory keeps growing until it hits Node's per-process memory limit and crashes, taking its other test files down too. All 13 crashed files pass alone. | 6 module + 7 HTTP test files | Locally, in a full unsharded run |

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Validate HTTP Types passes with 0 failures. The `AdminGetSalesSummaryParams` dates match the validator, and the 9 upstream mismatches are fixed by regenerating or correcting those types.
2. `@medusajs/icons` and `@medusajs/ui` unit tests pass. Only one React version is installed for the design-system packages' tests.
3. The `replace-zod-imports` codemod tests pass 10 runs in a row, without changing the process working directory.
4. The utils test database helper uses `DB_PORT` like the other test helpers, and `mikro-orm-repository.spec.ts` passes in the dev container.
5. The Redis engine's `race.spec.ts` passes 10 runs in a row within the full package integration run. The `test:integration` script runs every spec file even if an earlier one fails, and still exits with an error if any failed.
6. The full module and HTTP integration suites finish in the dev container with no worker memory crashes, using the commands given in the docs.
7. `CONTRIBUTING.md` or the dev container README lists the commands to run each suite locally, including any memory or shard settings needed for item 6.
8. On a clean `develop`, every suite passes in the dev container: lint, HTTP types, unit, package integration (fast and slow), module integration and HTTP integration.

## Scope
**Medium**. Each of the 6 fixes is small, but together they touch about 6 areas: 10 HTTP types in packages/core/types, the design-system packages' React dependency and the lockfile, a CLI codemod test, a utils test fixture, the Redis engine's test script, and the Jest settings for the module and HTTP integration suites. Each fix must also be checked by rerunning its suite, sometimes 10 times for the flaky tests, plus a short docs update on running the suites locally.

## Out of Scope
- New tests for existing features.
- Making the suites faster, beyond what's needed to fix the timeout in item 5.
- Changing feature code, except the HTTP type fixes in item 1.
- Docs, OAS and CLI-with-database workflows that weren't part of this run.

## Open Questions
- For the 9 upstream type mismatches, should we regenerate them with `generate:http-types --force`, or fix each type by hand? Regenerating is faster but may make larger changes than needed to the types package.
- Memory: should we set Jest's `workerIdleMemoryLimit` (restarts a worker once its memory passes a limit) in the integration Jest configs, or just document running locally with `--shard`?

--- COMMENTS ---

===== ISSUE 103 =====
Add Selective Product Duplication Options (created 2026-11-08T03:47:46Z) labels:

## User Story
As a store owner, I want to choose which product attributes are copied when duplicating a product so that I can quickly create similar products without having to manually remove or modify unnecessary information.

## User Scenario
Currently, duplicating a product copies a predefined set of its attributes without allowing the store owner to choose what gets included.

A store owner wants to create a new shirt based on an existing product but only wants to copy its basic information, images, and variants, not its prices or inventory quantities.

When the store owner selects the duplicate product action, a modal appears with checkboxes for optional attributes, including images, variants, prices, and inventory settings. Basic product information is always copied.

By default, images, variants, and prices are selected, while inventory quantities are excluded. Inventory settings, such as `manage_inventory` and `allow_backorder`, can be copied separately from actual stock quantities.

The store owner selects the desired attributes and confirms the duplication. The existing backend duplication workflow is modified to respect these selections, creating a new product containing only the requested information.

The duplicated product is always created as a draft to prevent accidental publication. After successful duplication, the store owner is redirected to the new product's details page, where they can review and edit it before publishing.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Selecting the duplicate product action opens a modal allowing the store owner to configure which attributes will be copied.
2. The modal provides checkboxes for images, variants, prices, and inventory settings. Basic product information is always included.
3. Images, variants, and prices are selected by default, while inventory quantities are never copied.
4. Inventory settings (`manage_inventory`, `allow_backorder`, etc.) are treated separately from inventory quantities, allowing settings to be copied without copying stock levels.
5. The existing duplicate product API endpoint accepts the selected duplication options.
6. The backend duplication workflow copies only the selected attributes, while ensuring the duplicated product remains valid.
7. Duplicated products receive new IDs, are always created as drafts, and do not modify the original product.
8. The duplication process handles dependencies between attributes, such as prices requiring corresponding variants.
9. Successful duplication redirects the store owner to the new product's details page. Failed duplication displays an error without redirecting.
10. Automated tests cover different combinations of duplication options, attribute dependencies, draft status, and duplication failures.

## Out of Scope
- Duplicating multiple products simultaneously.
- Changing the original product during duplication.
- Allowing individual variants or images to be selected.
- Copying inventory quantities from the original product.
- Redesigning the product creation or editing forms.
- Adding new product attributes or functionality unrelated to duplication.

## Open Questions
- Should deselecting variants automatically disable prices and inventory settings, or should these options remain visible but unavailable?
- Should the selected duplication options persist between duplication attempts, or reset to the defaults each time?

--- COMMENTS ---

===== 102 =====
## User Story
As a store owner, I want all changes made during a full product edit to be saved together so that my product data remains consistent even if an error occurs.

## User Scenario
This is a hardening issue intended to address technical debt introduced by the initial implementation of full product editing (PR #79). The existing feature saves changes through multiple sequential API requests rather than a single backend workflow. If a later request fails, earlier changes may have already been saved, leaving the product partially updated.

For example, a store owner modifies a product's subtitle, dimensions, and variant prices. If the variant updates succeed but the product update fails, only some of the changes are saved.

The goal is to replace this behavior with a unified backend workflow that ensures all changes are saved successfully or rolled back if an error occurs.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A new backend endpoint or workflow supports updating product details and existing variants through a single request.
2. The backend uses Medusa's workflow system with appropriate rollback or compensation mechanisms to prevent partial updates if any step fails.
3. The full product editing page uses the new backend endpoint instead of making multiple sequential requests.
4. Existing variants are identified using stable variant IDs rather than their positions in the editing form.
5. Failed updates return meaningful error responses, allowing the editing form to remain open with the user's unsaved changes.
6. Successful updates return the user to the product details page with all changes reflected.
7. Automated tests verify successful updates, failed updates, rollback behavior, and correct variant identification.

## Out of Scope
- Redesigning the full product editing interface.
- Adding new product fields or editing capabilities.
- Refactoring the shared product creation form or its schema.
- Supporting creation or deletion of variants beyond existing functionality.

## Open Questions
- Can Medusa's existing product workflows be extended, or is a custom workflow necessary?
- Which workflow steps support rollback, and where would custom compensation logic be required?
- Should the new endpoint accept the existing frontend payload structure or introduce a unified update schema?
- How should errors be handled if a rollback operation also fails?

===== 64 =====
## User Story
As a store admin, I want to view and cancel customer subscriptions in the admin dashboard so that I can answer customer questions and handle problems without database access.

## User Scenario
A customer emails support: "My coffee subscription stopped and I don't know why." A store admin opens the new Subscriptions page in the admin dashboard and filters by status "Failed." They find the customer's subscription and open it. It shows the product variant, the monthly interval, when it failed, and the reason: "Payment declined." The admin explains this to the customer. Later, a different customer calls asking to cancel their subscription because they can't log in. The admin searches for their subscription, opens it, clicks "Cancel subscription," confirms, and the status changes to Canceled immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The admin sidebar has a "Subscriptions" item that opens a subscription list page.
2. The list shows customer (name or email), product and variant, quantity, interval, status and next billing date, with pagination.
3. The list can be filtered by status (active, canceled, failed) and by customer.
4. Clicking a row opens a detail page showing all subscription fields, including canceled or failed date and failure reason, plus links to the customer and to the orders linked to that subscription.
5. Active subscriptions have a "Cancel subscription" action with a confirmation prompt. Cancelling reuses the existing `endSubscriptionWorkflow`, so it behaves the same as a customer cancelling.
6. The cancel action is not shown for subscriptions that are already canceled or failed. Trying it through the API returns a `NOT_ALLOWED` error.
7. The customer detail page has a section listing that customer's subscriptions.
8. New admin API routes: `GET /admin/subscriptions`, `GET /admin/subscriptions/:id` and `POST /admin/subscriptions/:id/cancel`, protected by admin authentication.
9. HTTP integration tests cover list filtering, detail retrieval, cancellation and the error for cancelling a subscription that isn't active. Dashboard tests cover the list, detail and cancel flow.

## Out of Scope
- Pausing or resuming subscriptions (this would need a new status and changes to renewal).
- Admins creating subscriptions or editing interval, quantity or variant.
- Retrying failed renewals or restarting canceled subscriptions.
- Changing the renewal schedule or the hourly job.

## Open Questions
- Should this issue also add a UI for choosing which intervals a variant offers? Today that is set only through `variant.metadata.subscription_intervals`, which admins can't easily edit.
- Should cancelling notify the customer (for example by email through the notification module), or is that a separate issue?

```text
     385 packages/core/core-flows/src/promotion/helpers/import-promotions.ts
     428 packages/core/core-flows/src/promotion/helpers/__tests__/import-promotions.spec.ts
     813 total
=== IMPORT HELPER ===
import type {
  CreatePromotionDTO,
  CreatePromotionRuleDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  ApplicationMethodAllocation,
  ApplicationMethodTargetType,
  ApplicationMethodType,
  MedusaError,
  PromotionRuleOperator,
  PromotionStatus,
  PromotionType,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { parse } from "csv-parse/sync"

/**
 * A promotion row read from an import CSV, numbered like a spreadsheet row
 * (the header is row 1).
 */
export type PromotionImportRow = {
  rowNumber: number
  code: string
  type: string
  status: string
  is_automatic: string
  is_tax_inclusive: string
  limit: string
  campaign_id: string
  discount_type: string
  value: string
  currency_code: string
  target_type: string
  allocation: string
  max_quantity: string
  buy_rules_min_quantity: string
  apply_to_quantity: string
  rules: string
  target_rules: string
  buy_rules: string
}

const COLUMNS: Record<
  Exclude<keyof PromotionImportRow, "rowNumber">,
  string
> = {
  code: "Code",
  type: "Type",
  status: "Status",
  is_automatic: "Automatic",
  is_tax_inclusive: "Tax Inclusive",
  limit: "Usage Limit",
  campaign_id: "Campaign ID",
  discount_type: "Discount Type",
  value: "Discount Value",
  currency_code: "Currency Code",
  target_type: "Target",
  allocation: "Allocation",
  max_quantity: "Max Quantity",
  buy_rules_min_quantity: "Buy Min Quantity",
  apply_to_quantity: "Apply To Quantity",
  rules: "Rules",
  target_rules: "Target Rules",
  buy_rules: "Buy Rules",
}

const REQUIRED_FIELDS = [
  "code",
  "type",
  "discount_type",
  "value",
  "target_type",
] as const

const BUYGET_REQUIRED_FIELDS = [
  "buy_rules",
  "target_rules",
  "buy_rules_min_quantity",
  "apply_to_quantity",
  "max_quantity",
] as const

const BOOLEAN_FIELDS = ["is_automatic", "is_tax_inclusive"] as const

const QUANTITY_FIELDS = [
  "max_quantity",
  "buy_rules_min_quantity",
  "apply_to_quantity",
] as const

const RULE_FIELDS = ["rules", "target_rules", "buy_rules"] as const

const OPERATORS: string[] = Object.values(PromotionRuleOperator)

/**
 * Parses an import CSV with the columns of the promotion import template.
 */
export const parsePromotionImportCsv = (
  fileContent: string
): PromotionImportRow[] => {
  let records: { record: Record<string, string>; info: { lines: number } }[]

  try {
    records = parse(fileContent, {
      columns: true,
      bom: true,
      skip_empty_lines: true,
      trim: true,
      info: true,
    })
  } catch (error) {
    throw new MedusaError(
      MedusaError.Types.INVALID_DATA,
      `The file could not be read as a CSV: ${error.message}`
    )
  }

  return records.map(({ record, info }) => {
    const row = { rowNumber: info.lines } as PromotionImportRow
    for (const [field, column] of Object.entries(COLUMNS)) {
      row[field] = record[column] ?? ""
    }
    return row
  })
}

const listFields = (names: string[]) =>
  names.length > 1
    ? `${names.slice(0, -1).join(", ")} and ${names[names.length - 1]}`
    : names[0]

const listOptions = (values: string[]) =>
  `${values.slice(0, -1).join(", ")} or ${values[values.length - 1]}`

/**
 * Parses a rule column in the form `attribute:operator:value1|value2`, with
 * rules separated by `;`. Returns the first rule that can't be read when the
 * column is invalid.
 */
const parseRules = (
  value: string
): { rules: CreatePromotionRuleDTO[] } | { invalid: string } => {
  const rules: CreatePromotionRuleDTO[] = []

  for (const rule of value.split(";").map((part) => part.trim())) {
    const [attribute, operator, ...rest] = rule.split(":")
    const values = rest
      .join(":")
      .split("|")
      .map((part) => part.trim())
      .filter(Boolean)

    if (!attribute?.trim() || !OPERATORS.includes(operator) || !values.length) {
      return { invalid: rule }
    }

    rules.push({
      attribute: attribute.trim(),
      operator: operator as CreatePromotionRuleDTO["operator"],
      values,
    })
  }

  return { rules }
}

/**
 * Checks a filled in enum column against its allowed options. Booleans are
 * matched ignoring case, like Requires Shipping in the inventory import.
 */
const checkOption = (
  row: PromotionImportRow,
  field: keyof typeof COLUMNS,
  options: string[]
) => {
  const value = BOOLEAN_FIELDS.includes(field as any)
    ? row[field].toLowerCase()
    : row[field]

  return value && !options.includes(value)
    ? `${COLUMNS[field]} must be ${listOptions(options)}, got "${row[field]}"`
    : undefined
}

/**
 * Checks every row and returns the promotions to create along with one error
 * per failing row. Codes are compared exactly, both within the file and
 * against `existingCodes`, and Campaign IDs are looked up in `campaignIds`.
 */
export const validatePromotionImport = (
  rows: PromotionImportRow[],
  existingCodes: string[],
  campaignIds: string[]
): { promotions: CreatePromotionDTO[]; errors: string[] } => {
  const existing = new Set(existingCodes)
  const campaigns = new Set(campaignIds)
  const firstRowByCode = new Map<string, number>()
  const promotions: CreatePromotionDTO[] = []
  const errors: string[] = []

  for (const row of rows) {
    const { rowNumber, code } = row

    const missing = REQUIRED_FIELDS.filter((field) => !row[field])
    if (missing.length) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: ${listFields(
          missing.map((field) => COLUMNS[field])
        )} ${missing.length > 1 ? "are" : "is"} required`
      )
      continue
    }

    const firstRow = firstRowByCode.get(code)
    if (firstRow) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: ${code} is also used on row ${firstRow} of this file`
      )
      continue
    }
    firstRowByCode.set(code, rowNumber)

    const badOption = [
      checkOption(row, "type", Object.values(PromotionType)),
      checkOption(row, "status", Object.values(PromotionStatus)),
      ...BOOLEAN_FIELDS.map((field) =>
        checkOption(row, field, ["true", "false"])
      ),
      checkOption(row, "discount_type", Object.values(ApplicationMethodType)),
      checkOption(
        row,
        "target_type",
        Object.values(ApplicationMethodTargetType)
      ),
      checkOption(
        row,
        "allocation",
        Object.values(ApplicationMethodAllocation)
      ),
    ].find(Boolean)
    if (badOption) {
      errors.push(`Row ${rowNumber}: ${badOption}`)
      continue
    }

    if (!Number.isFinite(Number(row.value))) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: Discount Value must be a number, got "${row.value}"`
      )
      continue
    }

    const badQuantity = QUANTITY_FIELDS.find(
      (field) => row[field] && !Number.isFinite(Number(row[field]))
    )
    if (badQuantity) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: ${COLUMNS[badQuantity]} must be a number, got "${row[badQuantity]}"`
      )
      continue
    }

    if (row.limit && !/^[1-9]\d*$/.test(row.limit)) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: Usage Limit must be a whole number of 1 or more, got "${row.limit}"`
      )
      continue
    }

    const value = Number(row.value)
    if (
      row.discount_type === ApplicationMethodType.PERCENTAGE &&
      (value <= 0 || value > 100)
    ) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: A percentage Discount Value must be greater than 0 and at most 100`
      )
      continue
    }

    const isAutomatic = row.is_automatic.toLowerCase() === "true"
    if (isAutomatic && row.limit) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: Automatic promotions cannot have a Usage Limit`
      )
      continue
    }

    if (row.type === PromotionType.BUYGET) {
      const missingBuyget = BUYGET_REQUIRED_FIELDS.filter(
        (field) => !row[field]
      )
      if (missingBuyget.length) {
        errors.push(
          `Row ${rowNumber}: buyget promotions require ${listFields(
            missingBuyget.map((field) => COLUMNS[field])
          )}`
        )
        continue
      }
    }

    const parsedRules: Partial<
      Record<(typeof RULE_FIELDS)[number], CreatePromotionRuleDTO[]>
    > = {}
    const badRule = RULE_FIELDS.filter((field) => row[field])
      .map((field) => {
        const parsed = parseRules(row[field])
        if ("invalid" in parsed) {
          return `${COLUMNS[field]} has an invalid rule "${parsed.invalid}"`
        }
        parsedRules[field] = parsed.rules
        return undefined
      })
      .find(Boolean)
    if (badRule) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: ${badRule}. Each rule must be attribute:operator:value1|value2 with an operator of ${listOptions(
          OPERATORS
        )}`
      )
      continue
    }

    if (row.campaign_id && !campaigns.has(row.campaign_id)) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: No campaign has the ID "${row.campaign_id}"`
      )
      continue
    }

    if (existing.has(code)) {
      errors.push(
        `Row ${rowNumber}: A promotion with the code ${code} already exists`
      )
      continue
    }

    const promotion: CreatePromotionDTO = {
      code,
      type: row.type as CreatePromotionDTO["type"],
      status: (row.status ||
        PromotionStatus.DRAFT) as CreatePromotionDTO["status"],
      application_method: {
        type: row.discount_type as ApplicationMethodType,
        value,
        target_type: row.target_type as ApplicationMethodTargetType,
      },
    }
    for (const field of BOOLEAN_FIELDS) {
      if (row[field]) {
        promotion[field] = row[field].toLowerCase() === "true"
      }
    }
    if (row.limit) {
      promotion.limit = Number(row.limit)
    }
    if (row.campaign_id) {
      promotion.campaign_id = row.campaign_id
    }
    if (parsedRules.rules) {
      promotion.rules = parsedRules.rules
    }
    if (row.currency_code) {
      promotion.application_method.currency_code = row.currency_code
    }
    if (row.allocation) {
      promotion.application_method.allocation =
        row.allocation as ApplicationMethodAllocation
    }
    for (const field of QUANTITY_FIELDS) {
      if (row[field]) {
        promotion.application_method[field] = Number(row[field])
      }
    }
    if (parsedRules.target_rules) {
      promotion.application_method.target_rules = parsedRules.target_rules
    }
    if (parsedRules.buy_rules) {
      promotion.application_method.buy_rules = parsedRules.buy_rules
    }
    promotions.push(promotion)
  }

  return { promotions, errors }
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-11-12 16:55:41Z)**_

Good question on the slice. Let me explain with the real code, then claim it.

## How the converter mirrors `import-promotions.ts`

`packages/core/core-flows/src/promotion/helpers/import-promotions.ts` is 385 lines doing CSV text to `CreatePromotionDTO`. The export is the inverse of that same file, and four pieces line up one to one:

**1. The column list already exists.** `COLUMNS` in that file maps each field to its header, in order:

```ts
const COLUMNS: Record<Exclude<keyof PromotionImportRow, "rowNumber">, string> = {
  code: "Code", type: "Type", status: "Status", is_automatic: "Automatic", ...
}
```

AC3 says the export must use the same headers in the same order. If I write that list out a second time, the two drift the first time anyone adds a column. So the slice exports `COLUMNS` from the import file and builds the header with `Object.values(COLUMNS)`. AC3 then holds by construction, not by a test watching two copies of a literal.

**2. `parseRules` inverts directly.** The import does:

```ts
const [attribute, operator, ...rest] = rule.split(":")
const values = rest.join(":").split("|").map(p => p.trim()).filter(Boolean)
```

The export is `${attribute}:${operator}:${values.join("|")}` joined with `;`. That is AC4, and it is about four lines.

**3. Booleans and empties.** The import reads `row[field].toLowerCase() === "true"` and defaults missing cells with `record[column] ?? ""`. The export writes `true`/`false` and an empty cell for null or undefined. That is AC5.

**4. The last 40 lines of `validatePromotionImport` are the thing to invert.** The block building `promotion.application_method.currency_code`, `allocation`, the three quantity fields, `target_rules` and `buy_rules` is exactly what the converter reads back out of a `PromotionDTO`. The import's shape is flat, 18 string fields. A promotion from the DB is nested under `application_method`. The converter flattens it.

The payoff is AC6, the round trip. Because `parsePromotionImportCsv` and `validatePromotionImport` are pure functions already covered by a 428 line Jest spec next door, the round trip test is: build a promotion, convert it to a row, feed the CSV straight back through those two functions, assert you get the same thing. No database, no HTTP server. The issue's strongest acceptance criterion is a plain unit test.

**Campaign ID: keep it, do not blank it.**

import { exportCustomersWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { FilterableCustomerProps, HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<{}, HttpTypes.AdminCustomerFilters>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminExportCustomersResponse>
) => {
  const selectFields = req.queryConfig.fields ?? []
  // filterableFields doesn't include limit and offset, so every customer
  // matching the filters is exported, not only the current page.
  const input = {
    select: selectFields,
    filter: req.filterableFields as FilterableCustomerProps,
  }

  const { transaction } = await exportCustomersWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input,
  })

  res.status(202).json({ transaction_id: transaction.transactionId })
}
```

Spec review, and I am taking this one. I wrote the import side in #41.

**Acceptance criteria.** All eight are clear and testable, and three of them are unusually easy to verify. AC3 lists the exact columns in order rather than saying "the same as the import", so a test can assert the header string. AC4 gives the rule format with a worked example. AC6 names `import-promotions.ts` as the thing to parse the export with, which turns the round trip into a plain unit test instead of a judgement call. AC8 already says which level each test belongs at.

**Cases I looked into.** Four, and the pattern this issue follows settles all of them, so I don't think the spec needs changes.

- Permissions. Medusa authenticates per namespace in `ApiLoader.#applyAuthMiddleware`, so `POST /admin/promotions/export` is admin-only without doing anything. The customer export route carries no auth code of its own.
- Exporting more than one page. This is the easy thing to get wrong, and the customer export route already solves it, with a comment saying so: `filterableFields` leaves out limit and offset, so the filter covers every match. AC2 is satisfied by following that route.
- A filter that matches nothing. This produces a file with only the header row. That is consistent with the customer export and still imports cleanly, so I am treating it as correct rather than an error case.
- The background job failing. AC7 covers the success notification. On failure the behavior is whatever the customer export does today, and changing that is a bigger question than this issue.

**Scope.** Medium is right. The customer export is about 19 files and this follows it closely. The only genuinely new code is converting a promotion and its nested rules into the flat 18 column row, which is why the unit and round trip tests in AC8 matter more here than the integration test.

Answers to the three open questions, since I am implementing it:

**Campaign ID: keep it, do not blank it.** The import already validates this column. `validatePromotionImport` checks the ID against the campaigns that exist and fails the row with `No campaign has the ID "camp_x"`, naming the row number. A file moved to another store fails loudly on exactly the rows that need attention, and the admin can clear the column and re-import. Blanking it on export would instead silently drop the campaign link on a same-store round trip, which is the more common case and the one AC6 tests.

**A rule the import cannot read back: export it anyway.** The operator is safe, since rules come out of the database with the enum already constrained and the import accepts every value of it. The real hazard is a rule value containing `;`, `|` or `:`, because `parseRules` splits on those, so the value exports fine and comes back wrong. I would rather export the promotion than skip or fail it, because the export's job is to show what is in the store, and skipping rows means the file quietly disagrees with the list the admin just filtered. In practice these values are IDs, currency codes and customer group IDs, none of which contain the delimiters. I will add a unit test that pins the behavior so it is documented rather than discovered, and record it in the PR's Tech Debt section. Inventing an escaping scheme is out, because the import cannot read it and that breaks AC6.

**Always use the import format.** AC3 fixes the columns and AC6 requires the round trip, and both only hold if there is one format. Promotion fields outside those columns, like usage counts and campaign budgets, are already out of scope.

One thing I am adding that is not in the ACs. The import's `COLUMNS` map is the single definition of the headers and their order, and it is currently private to that file. A file moved to another store fails loudly on exactly the rows that need attention, and the admin can clear the column and re-import. Blanking it on export would instead silently drop the campaign link on a same-store round trip, which is the more common case and the one AC6 tests.

**A rule the import cannot read back: export it anyway.** The operator is safe, since rules come out of the database with the enum already constrained and the import accepts every value of it. The real hazard is a rule value containing `;`, `|` or `:`, because `parseRules` splits on those, so the value exports fine and comes back wrong. I would rather export the promotion than skip or fail it, because the export's job is to show what is in the store, and skipping rows means the file quietly disagrees with the list the admin just filtered. ```text
=== export-customers step ===
import {
  CustomerDTO,
  FilterableCustomerProps,
  IFileModuleService,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  Modules,
  deduplicate,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { StepResponse, createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { json2csv } from "json-2-csv"

/**
 * The data to export customers.
 */
export type ExportCustomersStepInput = {
  /**
   * The number of customers to retrieve per batch.
   */
  batch_size?: number | string
  /**
   * The fields to select.
   */
  select: string[]
  /**
   * The filters to select which customers to export.
   */
  filter?: FilterableCustomerProps
}

/**
 * The details of the exported file.
 */
export type ExportCustomersStepOutput = {
  /**
   * The ID of the file.
   */
  id: string
  /**
   * The name of the file.
   */
  filename: string
}

export const exportCustomersStepId = "export-customers"

// The first five columns match the customer import CSV, so an exported file
// can be imported again.
const EXPORT_COLUMNS = [
  "Email",
  "First Name",
  "Last Name",
  "Company",
  "Phone",
  "Customer ID",
  "Has Account",
  "Created At",
]

const normalizeCustomerForExport = (customer: CustomerDTO): object => {
  return {
    Email: customer.email || "",
    "First Name": customer.first_name || "",
    "Last Name": customer.last_name || "",
    Company: customer.company_name || "",
    Phone: customer.phone || "",
    "Customer ID": customer.id,
    "Has Account": customer.has_account,
    "Created At": customer.created_at,
  }
}

/**
 * This step exports the customers matching the filters to a CSV file and
 * uploads it with the File Module. It retrieves the customers in batches, so
 * any pagination in the filters is ignored. The file always has a header row,
 * even when no customers match.
 */
export const exportCustomersStep = createStep(
  exportCustomersStepId,
  async (input: ExportCustomersStepInput, { container }) => {
    const query = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)
    const fileModule = container.resolve(Modules.FILE)

    const filename = `${Date.now()}-customer-exports.csv`
    const { writeStream, promise, fileKey } = await fileModule.getUploadStream({
      filename,
      mimeType: "text/csv",
    })

    const pageSize = !isNaN(parseInt(input?.batch_size as string))
      ? parseInt(input?.batch_size as string, 10)
      : 50

    let lastId: string | undefined
    let hasHeader = false

    const fields = deduplicate([
      ...input.select,
      "id",
      "email",
      "first_name",
      "last_name",
      "company_name",
      "phone",
      "has_account",
      "created_at",
    ])

    const filter = input.filter ?? {}

    while (true) {
      // Page with an id cursor instead of an offset, so customers sharing a
      // created_at, or added and deleted during the export, aren't skipped or
      // repeated. The cursor goes in $and so it can't replace an id filter.
      const { data: customers } = await query.graph({
        entity: "customer",
        filters: lastId
          ? {
              ...filter,
              $and: [...(filter.$and ?? []), { id: { $gt: lastId } }],
            }
          : filter,
        pagination: {
          take: pageSize,
          order: { id: "ASC" },
        },
        fields,
      })

      if (customers.length === 0) {
        break
      }

      const batchCsv = json2csv(
        customers.map((customer) =>
          normalizeCustomerForExport(customer as CustomerDTO)
        ),
        {
          keys: EXPORT_COLUMNS,
          prependHeader: !hasHeader,
          preventCsvInjection: true,
          emptyFieldValue: "",
        }
      )

      const ok = writeStream.write((hasHeader ? "\n" : "") + batchCsv)
      if (!ok) {
        await new Promise((resolve) => writeStream.once("drain", resolve))
      }

      hasHeader = true
      lastId = customers[customers.length - 1].id

      if (customers.length < pageSize) {
        break
      }
    }

    if (!hasHeader) {
      writeStream.write(EXPORT_COLUMNS.join(","))
    }

    writeStream.end()

    await promise

    return new StepResponse(
      { id: fileKey, filename } as ExportCustomersStepOutput,
      fileKey
    )
  },
  async (fileId, { container }) => {
    if (!fileId) {
      return
    }

    const fileModule: IFileModuleService = container.resolve(Modules.FILE)
    await fileModule.deleteFiles(fileId)
  }
)
```

=== product normalize-for-export ===
import {
  BigNumberInput,
  HttpTypes,
  PricingTypes,
  RegionTypes,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { MedusaError, upperCaseFirst } from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

/**
 * Normalizes product data for export, creating one row per product variant.
 * Products without variants will have a single row, while products with variants
 * will have one row per variant containing both product and variant data.
 *
 * @param product - The array of products to normalize for export.
 * @param regions - Object containing an array of region data used for price formatting.
 * @returns An array of normalized objects ready for export, with flattened product and variant data.
 *
 * @example
 * const normalizedData = normalizeForExport(
 *   [productA, productB],
 *   { regions: [region1, region2] }
 * )
 */
export const normalizeForExport = (
  product: HttpTypes.AdminProduct[],
  { regions }: { regions: RegionTypes.RegionDTO[] }
): object[] => {
  // Currently region names are treated as case-insensitive.
  const regionsMap = new Map(regions.map((r) => [r.id, r]))

  const res = product.reduce((acc: object[], product) => {
    const variants = product.variants ?? []
    if (!variants.length) {
      acc.push(normalizeProductForExport(product))
      return acc
    }

    variants.forEach((v) => {
      const toPush = {
        ...normalizeProductForExport(product),
        ...normalizeVariantForExport(v, regionsMap, product),
      } as any
      delete toPush["Product Variants"]

      acc.push(toPush)
    })

    return acc
  }, [])

  return res
}

const normalizeProductForExport = (product: HttpTypes.AdminProduct): object => {
  const flattenedImages = product.images?.reduce(
    (acc: Record<string, string>, image, idx) => {
      acc[beautifyKey(`product_image_${idx + 1}`)] = image.url
      return acc
    },
    {}
  )

  const flattenedTags = product.tags?.reduce(
    (acc: Record<string, string>, tag, idx) => {
      acc[beautifyKey(`product_tag_${idx + 1}`)] = tag.value
      return acc
    },
    {}
  )

Write export converter and check formatting

```bash
cd ~/medusa && cat > packages/core/core-flows/src/promotion/helpers/export-promotions.ts <<'EOF'
import type { PromotionDTO, PromotionRuleDTO } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { COLUMNS } from "./import-promotions"

/**
 * The export's columns, in the order the import template expects them.
 */
export const EXPORT_COLUMNS = Object.values(COLUMNS)

/**
 * Writes a rule list in the import's format, `attribute:operator:value1|value2`
 * with rules separated by `;`. Rules missing an attribute, an operator or every
 * value are left out, since the import can't read them back.
 */
const serializeRules = (rules?: PromotionRuleDTO[]): string =>
  (rules ?? [])
    .map((rule) => {
      const values = (rule.values ?? [])
        .map((ruleValue) => ruleValue.value)
        .filter((value): value is string => !!value)

      if (!rule.attribute || !rule.operator || !values.length) {
        return undefined
      }

      return `${rule.attribute}:${rule.operator}:${values.join("|")}`
    })
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(";")

/**
 * Writes a value the import reads as a boolean. A promotion that has never had
 * the flag set exports an empty cell rather than `false`, which the import
 * treats the same way.
 */
const serializeBoolean = (value?: boolean): string =>
  typeof value === "boolean" ? String(value) : ""

const serializeNumber = (value?: number | null): string =>
  typeof value === "number" ? String(value) : ""

/**
 * Flattens a promotion and its application method into one row of the import
 * template, keyed by column name. Fields the promotion doesn't have become
 * empty cells, so the row can be read back by `parsePromotionImportCsv` and
 * `validatePromotionImport`.
 */
export const normalizePromotionForExport = (
  promotion: PromotionDTO
): Record<string, string> => {
  const applicationMethod = promotion.application_method

  return {
    [COLUMNS.code]: promotion.code ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.type]: promotion.type ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.status]: promotion.status ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.is_automatic]: serializeBoolean(promotion.is_automatic),
    [COLUMNS.is_tax_inclusive]: serializeBoolean(promotion.is_tax_inclusive),
    [COLUMNS.limit]: serializeNumber(promotion.limit),
    [COLUMNS.campaign_id]: promotion.campaign_id ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.discount_type]: applicationMethod?.type ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.value]: serializeNumber(applicationMethod?.value),
    [COLUMNS.currency_code]: applicationMethod?.currency_code ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.target_type]: applicationMethod?.target_type ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.allocation]: applicationMethod?.allocation ?? "",
    [COLUMNS.max_quantity]: serializeNumber(applicationMethod?.max_quantity),
    [COLUMNS.buy_rules_min_quantity]: serializeNumber(
      applicationMethod?.buy_rules_min_quantity
    ),
    [COLUMNS.apply_to_quantity]: serializeNumber(
      applicationMethod?.apply_to_quantity
    ),
    [COLUMNS.rules]: serializeRules(promotion.rules),
    [COLUMNS.target_rules]: serializeRules(applicationMethod?.target_rules),
    [COLUMNS.buy_rules]: serializeRules(applicationMethod?.buy_rules),
  }
}
EOF
