```bash
cd ~/medusa && cat > packages/core/core-flows/src/promotion/helpers/__tests__/export-promotions.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import type {
  PromotionDTO,
  PromotionRuleDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import { json2csv } from "json-2-csv"
import {
  EXPORT_COLUMNS,
  normalizePromotionForExport,
} from "../export-promotions"
import {
  parsePromotionImportCsv,
  validatePromotionImport,
} from "../import-promotions"

// The header the import template defines, written out rather than built from
// the code so a column that moves or is renamed fails this test.
const HEADER =
  "Code,Type,Status,Automatic,Tax Inclusive,Usage Limit,Campaign ID,Discount Type,Discount Value,Currency Code,Target,Allocation,Max Quantity,Buy Min Quantity,Apply To Quantity,Rules,Target Rules,Buy Rules"

const rule = (
  attribute: string,
  operator: string,
  ...values: string[]
): PromotionRuleDTO =>
  ({
    id: `prule_${attribute}`,
    attribute,
    operator,
    values: values.map((value) => ({ id: `pruleval_${value}`, value })),
  } as PromotionRuleDTO)

const STANDARD: PromotionDTO = {
  id: "promo_1",
  code: "SAVE10",
  type: "standard",
  status: "active",
  is_automatic: false,
  is_tax_inclusive: false,
  campaign_id: "camp_1",
  application_method: {
    id: "proappmet_1",
    type: "percentage",
    value: 10,
    target_type: "items",
    allocation: "across",
  },
  rules: [rule("currency_code", "eq", "eur")],
} as PromotionDTO

const BUYGET: PromotionDTO = {
  id: "promo_2",
  code: "BUY2GET1",
  type: "buyget",
  status: "draft",
  application_method: {
    id: "proappmet_2",
    type: "percentage",
    value: 100,
    target_type: "items",
    allocation: "each",
    max_quantity: 1,
    buy_rules_min_quantity: 2,
    apply_to_quantity: 1,
    target_rules: [rule("product_id", "in", "prod_1")],
    buy_rules: [rule("product_id", "eq", "prod_2")],
  },
} as PromotionDTO

const toCsv = (promotions: PromotionDTO[]) =>
  json2csv(promotions.map(normalizePromotionForExport), {
    keys: EXPORT_COLUMNS,
    prependHeader: true,
    preventCsvInjection: true,
    emptyFieldValue: "",
  })

describe("normalizePromotionForExport", () => {
  it("uses the import template's columns in the template's order", () => {
    expect(EXPORT_COLUMNS.join(",")).toEqual(HEADER)
  })

  it("flattens a promotion and its application method into one row", () => {
    expect(normalizePromotionForExport(STANDARD)).toEqual({
      Code: "SAVE10",
      Type: "standard",
      Status: "active",
      Automatic: "false",
      "Tax Inclusive": "false",
      "Usage Limit": "",
      "Campaign ID": "camp_1",
      "Discount Type": "percentage",
      "Discount Value": "10",
      "Currency Code": "",
      Target: "items",
      Allocation: "across",
      "Max Quantity": "",
      "Buy Min Quantity": "",
      "Apply To Quantity": "",
      Rules: "currency_code:eq:eur",
      "Target Rules": "",
      "Buy Rules": "",
    })
  })

  it("joins a rule's values with | and separate rules with ;", () => {
    const promotion = {
      ...STANDARD,
      rules: [
        rule("currency_code", "eq", "eur"),
        rule("customer_group_id", "in", "cg_1", "cg_2"),
      ],
    } as PromotionDTO

    expect(normalizePromotionForExport(promotion).Rules).toEqual(
      "currency_code:eq:eur;customer_group_id:in:cg_1|cg_2"
    )
  })

  it("writes the buyget quantities and both rule columns", () => {
    const row = normalizePromotionForExport(BUYGET)

    expect(row["Max Quantity"]).toEqual("1")
    expect(row["Buy Min Quantity"]).toEqual("2")
    expect(row["Apply To Quantity"]).toEqual("1")
    expect(row["Target Rules"]).toEqual("product_id:in:prod_1")
    expect(row["Buy Rules"]).toEqual("product_id:eq:prod_2")
  })

  it("leaves a field the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell", () => {
    const row = normalizePromotionForExport({
      id: "promo_3",
      code: "BARE",
    } as PromotionDTO)

    expect(row).toEqual(
      Object.fromEntries(
        EXPORT_COLUMNS.map((column) => [
          column,
          column === "Code" ? "BARE" : "",
        ])
      )
    )
  })

  it("writes a limit of 0 and a value of 0 rather than treating them as unset", () => {
    const row = normalizePromotionForExport({
      ...STANDARD,
      limit: 0,
      application_method: { ...STANDARD.application_method, value: 0 },
    } as PromotionDTO)

    expect(row["Usage Limit"]).toEqual("0")
    expect(row["Discount Value"]).toEqual("0")
  })

  it("leaves out a rule with no values, which the import can't read back", () => {
    const promotion = {
      ...STANDARD,
      rules: [
        rule("currency_code", "eq"),
        rule("customer_group_id", "in", "cg_1"),
      ],
    } as PromotionDTO

    expect(normalizePromotionForExport(promotion).Rules).toEqual(
      "customer_group_id:in:cg_1"
    )
  })
})

describe("exported promotions read back through the import", () => {
  it("recreates a standard promotion with the same settings and rules", () => {
    const rows = parsePromotionImportCsv(toCsv([STANDARD]))
    const { promotions, errors } = validatePromotionImport(rows, [], ["camp_1"])

    expect(errors).toEqual([])
    expect(promotions).toEqual([
      {
        code: "SAVE10",
        type: "standard",
        status: "active",
        is_automatic: false,
        is_tax_inclusive: false,
        campaign_id: "camp_1",
        application_method: {
          type: "percentage",
          value: 10,
          target_type: "items",
          allocation: "across",
        },
        rules: [
          { attribute: "currency_code", operator: "eq", values: ["eur"] },
        ],
      },
    ])
  })

  it("recreates a buyget promotion with its quantities and both rule sets", () => {
    const rows = parsePromotionImportCsv(toCsv([BUYGET]))
    const { promotions, errors } = validatePromotionImport(rows, [], [])

    expect(errors).toEqual([])
    expect(promotions).toEqual([
      {
        code: "BUY2GET1",
        type: "buyget",
        status: "draft",
        application_method: {
          type: "percentage",
          value: 100,
          target_type: "items",
          allocation: "each",
          max_quantity: 1,
          buy_rules_min_quantity: 2,
          apply_to_quantity: 1,
          target_rules: [
            { attribute: "product_id", operator: "in", values: ["prod_1"] },
          ],
          buy_rules: [
            { attribute: "product_id", operator: "eq", values: ["prod_2"] },
          ],
        },
      },
    ])
  })

  it("exports every promotion in the file, one row each", () => {
    const rows = parsePromotionImportCsv(toCsv([STANDARD, BUYGET]))

    expect(rows).toHaveLength(2)
    expect(rows.map((row) => row.code)).toEqual(["SAVE10", "BUY2GET1"])
  })

  // Known limitation, recorded on #97: the import splits rule values on these
  // characters, so a value containing one is read back as a different rule.
  // Rule values are IDs and currency codes in practice.
  it("does not round trip a rule value containing a delimiter", () => {
    const promotion = {
      ...STANDARD,
      rules: [rule("customer_group_id", "in", "cg|1")],
    } as PromotionDTO

    const rows = parsePromotionImportCsv(toCsv([promotion]))
    const { promotions } = validatePromotionImport(rows, [], ["camp_1"])

    expect(promotions[0].rules).toEqual([
      { attribute: "customer_group_id", operator: "in", values: ["cg", "1"] },
    ])
  })
})
EOF

Commits on the medusa course repo: plain imperative subject line only, no body, no Co-Authored-By line, no feat()/fix()/test() prefixes. The changeset is the one exception and is its own commit titled "chore: add changeset for <thing>". Order commits tests first, then the code, then the changeset.

MEMORY.md
stick-to-acceptance-criteria.md
=== pr-41 description ===
Closes #41

What: Adds a promotion CSV import. There's an Import button on the Promotions list that opens a drawer where you can upload a CSV or download the template. Each row creates one promotion, including its rules. If any row is invalid, nothing is created and the drawer lists the failing rows by row number.

Why: Promotions could only be created one at a time, which doesn't work for someone moving a store with hundreds of them.

How: It works the same way as the customer and inventory imports. A new importPromotionsWorkflow checks every row first, then creates all the promotions with one createPromotionsWorkflow call, so it's all or nothing. The reasoning is in the Design section on #41. Along with the AC6 rules, it also checks the basics the API create validator enforces, like required fields and allowed values, since AC6 covers the rules the API enforces. A few rules that only the promotion module checks, like a fixed discount needing a currency, are still caught by the workflow, just without a row number. A blank Status defaults to draft, and the upload uses the same 1 MB limit as the other imports.

Testing: The tests are in the first three commits, before the code, and they failed before it because the route and drawer didn't exist yet.
- Helper tests in core-flows cover parsing, each validation rule, and reporting every failing row.
- Integration tests cover a valid file creating every promotion with its rules, one bad row creating none, and an existing code being rejected.
- Dashboard tests cover the Import button, the drawer, the template, the row error list and the 1 MB limit.

To run them:
yarn workspace @medusajs/core-flows test src/promotion/helpers
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test promotion-import promotion-list-table
yarn build, then with Postgres running: cd integration-tests/http && DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=postgres DB_PASSWORD=postgres npx jest __tests__/promotions/admin/ (use your own DB_PORT)

All of them pass, along with the existing promotion integration tests, and the dashboard typecheck is clean. The full dashboard suite has one failure, "en.json should not have extra keys", which already fails on develop.

CI doesn't run on PRs in this repo, so the local runs above stand in for it.

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The import repeats rules that the API and promotion module already check, so if those change, the import has to be updated too.

**Encountered:** The 1 MB upload limit is still only checked in the browser, like the other imports, so the route itself accepts bigger files.
```

Closes #97

What: Starts the promotion CSV export. This first part is the conversion itself, a helper that flattens a promotion and its application method into one row of the promotion import template, plus its unit tests. The route, the background workflow and step, the SDK method and the Export action on the Promotions list are still to come on this branch this week.

Why: Promotions can be imported but not exported, so there's no way to review them in a spreadsheet, keep a backup, or move them to another store. My spec review and the answers to the issue's open questions are on #97.

How: It follows the customer export, which keeps the conversion in a plain function returning an object keyed by column name and lets the step hand that to json2csv. The export's columns come from the import's own COLUMNS map rather than a second copy of the list, so the two can't drift when a column is added later. That meant exporting COLUMNS from import-promotions.ts, which is the only change to the import side. Rules are written back in the import's attribute:operator:value1|value2 form, booleans as true and false, and anything the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell. A rule with no readable values is left out instead of being written in a form the import would reject.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC3: Same column headers, in the same order, as the import template | `export-promotions.spec.ts > uses the import template's columns in the template's order` | unit | AC. The header is written out as a string literal in the test from the list in AC3, not read from the code |
| AC4: Rules use `attribute:operator:value`, values joined by `\|`, rules joined by `;` | `> joins a rule's values with \| and separate rules with ;`, `> writes the buyget quantities and both rule columns` | unit | AC. The expected string is AC4's own worked example |
| AC5: Empty fields are empty cells, booleans are `true`/`false` | `> flattens a promotion and its application method into one row`, `> leaves a field the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell`, `> writes a limit of 0 and a value of 0 rather than treating them as unset` | unit | AC |
| AC6: Importing an exported file recreates the promotion, checked with the existing import parser | `> recreates a standard promotion with the same settings and rules`, `> recreates a buyget promotion with its quantities and both rule sets`, `> exports every promotion in the file, one row each` | unit | AC. The expected `CreatePromotionDTO` is written out by hand from the source promotion, not captured from a run |
| AC1, AC2, AC7 | Not in this part of the branch yet. They land with the route, workflow and Export action | - | - |
| AC8: Unit, HTTP integration and dashboard tests | Unit tests done. The integration and dashboard tests come with the route and the Export action | unit | AC |

Not tested automatically, and why: nothing here is manual. The parts that need a running store are AC1, AC2 and AC7, and they are not in this part of the branch.

AI-written tests: the converter and this spec file were drafted with Claude Code. The expected values were not taken from the code's output. The header string and the rule examples are copied from AC3 and AC4 in the issue, and the round trip's expected `CreatePromotionDTO` is written out from the source promotion by hand. To check the tests actually bite, I changed the converter five ways and confirmed each failed something: joining rule values with a comma instead of `|`, joining rules with a comma instead of `;`, never writing booleans, dropping `campaign_id`, and never writing numbers. The first of those originally failed only one test, because every round trip fixture had single-value rules, so `join(",")` and `join("|")` gave the same string. I changed the standard round trip to use AC4's two-rule example, which has a rule with two values, and it now catches that change too.

To run them:
yarn workspace @medusajs/core-flows test -- promotion/helpers

Both helper specs pass, 52 tests. That includes the existing 40 import tests unchanged, which is the check that exporting COLUMNS broke nothing. CI doesn't run on PRs in this repo, so that run stands in for it.

## Tech Debt

Introduced: a rule value containing `;`, `|` or `:` exports fine but is read back as a different rule, because the import splits on those characters. In practice these values are IDs and currency codes. There's a test pinning the behavior so it's documented rather than discovered, and the reasoning is in my comment on #97. Fixing it properly means an escaping scheme on both sides, which would be its own issue.

Encountered: the export is tied to the import's template by design, so a promotion field that the template doesn't have a column for can't be exported at all. Usage counts, campaign details and campaign budgets are the ones that come up, and they're listed as out of scope on the issue.

# Sprint 2 Mid-Sprint Check-in - angrapsas

## What did you implement so far in the sprint, and what remains?

So far this sprint has mostly been planning for me instead of code. I broke down my two large issues from last sprint. #16 turned into #66 (medium) and #67 (small), and #23 turned into #68 and #69, which are both medium. While I was looking through the workflow engines to split #16, I found out they already have a cleanup job that deletes old executions, so the issue ended up being smaller than I originally wrote it. Nicholas has already picked up #66 and #67. I also got my customer and inventory imports from Sprint 1 running locally so I could take screenshots and get my part of the Lightning Talk ready.

What's left is the actual implementation. I'm taking #41 (promotion CSV import), #58 (handle inventory errors when completing a cart) and #63 (duplicate a promotion). I'm starting with #41 since it can reuse the same import setup I built for customers and inventory, then #63, then #58.

## What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?

I learned how Medusa decides whether a workflow runs right away or in the background. It's the same workflow engine either way. The product import marks a couple of its steps as async, so the workflow pauses there and the route sends back a response right away. Then a separate confirm route picks it back up and the rest gets processed in the background. My imports don't have any async steps, so the route just waits for the whole thing to finish, and since everything gets created in one database transaction, it either all goes in or nothing does.

The bigger thing I learned is that you really have to read the code before you trust an issue's scope. Last sprint #32 turned out to already exist, and this sprint #16 was smaller than I wrote it because the cleanup was already there. Both times I only figured that out by actually looking at the code.

## What is one thing you would do differently?

I would claim my issues right at the start of the sprint instead of halfway through. Last sprint pretty much all of my coding, reviews and merges happened in the last couple days, and I'm kind of doing the same thing again. I spent the first half of this sprint on planning and the presentation, and I'm only now picking up the issues I'm actually going to implement.

Claiming them earlier would have given me time to get my specs looked at before I started coding, which I mostly did late last sprint. It would also give my teammates more time to review instead of me asking for approvals on the day it's due. For the rest of this sprint I'm going to update the specs on #41, #58 and #63 and get someone to look at them before I start, and try to get my first PR up early enough that there's time to fix whatever comes up in review.

# Sprint 3 Mid-Sprint Check-in - angrapsas

## What have you implemented so far, and what remains?

I'm on #97, export promotions to CSV. Before writing anything I posted a spec review on the issue and answered its three open questions, since I wrote the import side in #41 and had opinions about what the export should do with campaign IDs and with rules the import can't read back.

PR #108 is open. It's the conversion itself, a helper that flattens a promotion and its application method into one row of the import template, with unit tests. The round trip test reads the exported row back with the existing import parser, which is the acceptance criterion I cared most about.

What remains on that branch is the admin route, the background workflow and step, the SDK method and the Export action on the Promotions list, plus the integration and dashboard tests. I also still need a second medium issue and a small one, and I expect at least one of those to come out of the team feature once we split it.

## What is one thing you learned about testing in your project?

That a test passing doesn't mean it would notice if the code were wrong.

My converter joins a promotion rule's values with a pipe. After my tests passed I changed that pipe to a comma to see what would break, and almost nothing did. Only one test failed. The reason was that every promotion I'd set up as a fixture had rules with a single value, so joining with a comma and joining with a pipe produced exactly the same string. The tests couldn't tell the two apart, including the round trip test I thought was the strong one.

I changed one fixture to use the two-value example from the acceptance criteria, and now two tests catch it. I'd never have found that by reading the tests or by running them, only by changing the code and watching what didn't fail. That's the whole idea behind the mutation testing deliverable, and finding it by hand first made that make a lot more sense.

## What is one risk to finishing your work by Nov 19, and what will you do about it?

The risk is getting stuck on the new requirements instead of on the code. Mutation testing is the one I'm worried about. Nobody on the team has StrykerJS running, there's nothing in the repo to copy, grad students need two submissions, and the tool refuses to start if any of the tests it selects already fail, which on this repo is a real possibility.

So I'm not leaving it until the PRs are done. @@ -0,0 +1,121 @@
+import { FilterableCustomerProps } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
+import {
+  WorkflowData,
+  createWorkflow,
+  transform,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
+import { useRemoteQueryStep } from "../../common"
+import { notifyOnFailureStep, sendNotificationsStep } from "../../notification"
+import { exportCustomersStep } from "../steps/export-customers"
+
+/**
+ * The data to export customers.
+ */
+export type ExportCustomersWorkflowInput = {
+  /**
+   * The fields to select. These fields will be passed to
+   * [Query](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/module-links/query).
+   */
+  select: string[]
+  /**
+   * The filters to select which customers to export.
+   */
+  filter?: FilterableCustomerProps
+}
+
+export const exportCustomersWorkflowId = "export-customers"
+/**
+ * This workflow exports customers matching the specified filters to a CSV
+ * file. It runs in the background.
+ *
+ * :::note
+ *
+ * This workflow doesn't return the exported customers. Instead, it sends a notification to the admin
+ * users that they can download the exported customers.
+ *
+ * :::
+ *
+ * @example
+ * To export all customers:
+ *
+ * ```ts
+ * const { transaction } = await exportCustomersWorkflow(container)
+ * .run({
+ *   input: {
+ *     select: ["*"],
+ *   }
+ * })
+ * ```
+ *
+ * To export customers matching a criteria:
+ *
+ * ```ts
+ * const { transaction } = await exportCustomersWorkflow(container)
+ * .run({
+ *   input: {
+ *     select: ["*"],
+ *     filter: {
+ *       has_account: false
+ *     }
+ *   }
+ * })
+ * ```
+ *
+ * @summary
+ *
+ * Export customers to a CSV file.
+ */
+export const exportCustomersWorkflow = createWorkflow(
+  exportCustomersWorkflowId,
+  (input: WorkflowData<ExportCustomersWorkflowInput>): WorkflowData<void> => {
+    const file = exportCustomersStep(input).config({
+      async: true,
+      backgroundExecution: true,
+    })
+
+    const failureNotification = transform({ input }, (data) => {
+      return [
+        {
+          // We don't need the recipient here for now, but if we want to push feed notifications to a specific user we could add it.
+          to: "",
+          channel: "feed",
+          template: "admin-ui",
+          data: {
+            title: "Customer export",
+            description: `Failed to export customers, please try again later.`,
+          },
+        },
+      ]
+    })
+    notifyOnFailureStep(failureNotification)
+
+    const fileDetails = useRemoteQueryStep({
+      fields: ["id", "url"],
+      entry_point: "file",
+      variables: { id: file.id },
+      list: false,
+    })
+
+    const notifications = transform({ fileDetails, file }, (data) => {
+      return [
+        {
+          // We don't need the recipient here for now, but if we want to push feed notifications to a specific user we could add it.
+          to: "",
+          channel: "feed",
+          template: "admin-ui",
+          data: {
+            title: "Customer export",
+            description: "Customer export completed successfully!",
+            file: {
+              filename: data.file.filename,
+              url: data.fileDetails.url,
+              mimeType: "text/csv",
+            },
+          },
+        },
+      ]
+    })
+
+    sendNotificationsStep(notifications)
+  }
+)

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,25 @@
+import { exportCustomersWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
+import {
+  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
+  MedusaResponse,
+} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
+import { FilterableCustomerProps, HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
+
+export const POST = async (
+  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<{}, HttpTypes.AdminCustomerFilters>,
+  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminExportCustomersResponse>
+) => {
+  const selectFields = req.queryConfig.fields ?? []
+  // filterableFields doesn't include limit and offset, so every customer
+  // matching the filters is exported, not only the current page.
+  const input = {
+    select: selectFields,
+    filter: req.filterableFields as FilterableCustomerProps,
+  }
+
+  const { transaction } = await exportCustomersWorkflow(req.scope).run({
+    input,
+  })
+
+  res.status(202).json({ transaction_id: transaction.transactionId })
+}

import { Button, Heading, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { RouteDrawer, useRouteModal } from "../../../components/modals"
import { useExportCustomers } from "../../../hooks/api/customers"
import { useCustomerTableQuery } from "../../../hooks/table/query"

export const CustomerExport = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <RouteDrawer>
      <RouteDrawer.Header>
        <RouteDrawer.Title asChild>
          <Heading>{t("customers.export.header")}</Heading>
        </RouteDrawer.Title>
        <RouteDrawer.Description className="sr-only">
          {t("customers.export.description")}
        </RouteDrawer.Description>
      </RouteDrawer.Header>
      <CustomerExportContent />
    </RouteDrawer>
  )
}

const CustomerExportContent = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  // The list's Export link forwards its query string, so this reads the same
  // filters and search that are applied to the customer list.
  const { searchParams } = useCustomerTableQuery({})

  const { mutateAsync } = useExportCustomers(searchParams)
  const { handleSuccess } = useRouteModal()

  const handleExportRequest = async () => {
    await mutateAsync(searchParams, {
      onSuccess: () => {
        // The export runs in a background workflow, so the response only
        // contains its transaction ID. The CSV's download URL arrives later as
        // a notification.
        toast.info(t("customers.export.success.title"), {
          description: t("customers.export.success.description"),
        })
        handleSuccess()
      },
      onError: (err) => {
        toast.error(err.message)
      },
    })
  }

  return (
    <>
      <RouteDrawer.Body>
        <p className="text-ui-fg-subtle text-sm">
          {t("customers.export.description")}
        </p>
      </RouteDrawer.Body>
      <RouteDrawer.Footer>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
          <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
            <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
              {t("actions.cancel")}
            </Button>
          </RouteDrawer.Close>
          <Button onClick={handleExportRequest} size="small">
            {t("actions.export")}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </RouteDrawer.Footer>
    </>
  )
}
```

+  const asLocalPath = filePath.replace("http://localhost:9000", os.tmpdir())
+  const fileContent = await fs.readFile(asLocalPath, { encoding: "utf-8" })
+  await fs.rm(path.dirname(asLocalPath), { recursive: true, force: true })
+  return csv2json(fileContent) as Record<string, unknown>[]
+}

import { PencilSquare, SquareTwoStack, Trash } from "@medusajs/icons"
import { AdminPromotion } from "@medusajs/types"
import { Button, Container, Heading, usePrompt } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { createColumnHelper } from "@tanstack/react-table"
import { useMemo } from "react"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { Link, Outlet, useLoaderData, useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"

import { keepPreviousData } from "@tanstack/react-query"
import { ActionMenu } from "../../../../../components/common/action-menu"
import { _DataTable } from "../../../../../components/table/data-table"
import {
  useDeletePromotion,
  usePromotions,
} from "../../../../../hooks/api/promotions"
import { usePromotionTableColumns } from "../../../../../hooks/table/columns/use-promotion-table-columns"
import { usePromotionTableFilters } from "../../../../../hooks/table/filters/use-promotion-table-filters"
import { usePromotionTableQuery } from "../../../../../hooks/table/query/use-promotion-table-query"
import { useDataTable } from "../../../../../hooks/use-data-table"
import { promotionsLoader } from "../../loader"

const PAGE_SIZE = 20

export const PromotionListTable = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const initialData = useLoaderData() as Awaited<
    ReturnType<ReturnType<typeof promotionsLoader>>
  >

  const { searchParams, raw } = usePromotionTableQuery({ pageSize: PAGE_SIZE })
  const { promotions, count, isLoading, isError, error } = usePromotions(
    { ...searchParams },
    {
      initialData,
      placeholderData: keepPreviousData,
    }
  )

  const filters = usePromotionTableFilters()
  const columns = useColumns()

  const { table } = useDataTable({
    data: (promotions ?? []) as AdminPromotion[],
    columns,
    count,
    enablePagination: true,
    pageSize: PAGE_SIZE,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
  })

  if (isError) {
    throw error
  }

  return (
    <Container className="divide-y p-0">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4">
        <Heading level="h1">{t("promotions.domain")}</Heading>

        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
          <Button size="small" variant="secondary" asChild>
            <Link to="import">{t("actions.import")}</Link>
          </Button>
          <Button size="small" variant="secondary" asChild>
            <Link to="create">{t("actions.create")}</Link>
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <_DataTable
        table={table}
        columns={columns}
        count={count}
        pageSize={PAGE_SIZE}
        filters={filters}
        search
        pagination
        isLoading={isLoading}
        queryObject={raw}
        navigateTo={(row) => `${row.original.id}`}
        orderBy={[
          { key: "created_at", label: t("fields.createdAt") },
          { key: "updated_at", label: t("fields.updatedAt") },
        ]}
      />
      <Outlet />
    </Container>
  )
}

import { Trash } from "@medusajs/icons"
import { Button, Heading, Hint, Text, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useMemo, useState } from "react"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"

import { FilePreview } from "../../../components/common/file-preview"
import {
  FileType,
  FileUpload,
  RejectedFile,
} from "../../../components/common/file-upload"
import { RouteDrawer, useRouteModal } from "../../../components/modals"
import { useImportPromotions } from "../../../hooks/api/promotions"
import { formatFileSize } from "../../../lib/format-file-size"
import { getPromotionImportCsvTemplate } from "./helpers/import-template"

const SUPPORTED_FORMATS = ["text/csv", "application/vnd.ms-excel"]

export const PromotionImport = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <RouteDrawer>
      <RouteDrawer.Header>
        <RouteDrawer.Title asChild>
          <Heading>{t("promotions.import.header")}</Heading>
        </RouteDrawer.Title>
        <RouteDrawer.Description className="sr-only">
          {t("promotions.import.description")}
        </RouteDrawer.Description>
      </RouteDrawer.Header>
      <PromotionImportContent />
    </RouteDrawer>
  )
}

const PromotionImportContent = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const [file, setFile] = useState<File>()
  const [fileError, setFileError] = useState<string>()
  const [rowErrors, setRowErrors] = useState<string[]>([])

  const { mutateAsync: importPromotions, isPending } = useImportPromotions()
  const { handleSuccess } = useRouteModal()

  const templateContent = useMemo(() => {
    return getPromotionImportCsvTemplate()
  }, [])

  const handleUploaded = (
    files: FileType[],
    rejectedFiles?: RejectedFile[]
  ) => {
    setRowErrors([])

    if (rejectedFiles?.length) {
      setFile(undefined)
      setFileError(
        t("promotions.import.fileTooLarge", {
          size: formatFileSize(__MAX_UPLOAD_FILE_SIZE__ ?? 1024 * 1024),
        })
      )
      return
    }

    setFileError(undefined)
    setFile(files[0]?.file)
  }

  const handleImport = async () => {
    if (!file) {
      return
    }

    setRowErrors([])

    await importPromotions(
      { file },
      {
        onSuccess: ({ created }) => {
          toast.success(t("promotions.import.successToast", { count: created }))
          handleSuccess()
        },
        onError: (err) => {
          // The API returns one line per failing row.
          setRowErrors(err.message.split("\n"))
        },
      }
    ).catch(() => {
      // Already handled in onError.
    })
  }

  const uploadedFileActions = [
    {
      actions: [
        {
          label: t("actions.delete"),
          icon: <Trash />,
          onClick: () => {
            setFile(undefined)
            setRowErrors([])
          },
        },
      ],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <>
      <RouteDrawer.Body>
        <Heading level="h2">{t("promotions.import.upload.title")}</Heading>
        <Text size="small" className="text-ui-fg-subtle">
          {t("promotions.import.upload.description")}
        </Text>

        <div className="mt-4">
          {file ? (
            <FilePreview
              filename={file.name}
              loading={isPending}
              activity={t("promotions.import.upload.importing")}
              actions={uploadedFileActions}
            />
          ) : (
            <div className="flex flex-col gap-y-4">
              <FileUpload
                label={t("promotions.import.uploadLabel")}
                hint={t("promotions.import.uploadHint")}
                multiple={false}
                hasError={!!fileError}
                formats={SUPPORTED_FORMATS}
                onUploaded={handleUploaded}
              />
              {fileError && (
                <div>
                  <Hint variant="error">{fileError}</Hint>
                </div>
              )}
            </div>
          )}
        </div>

        {rowErrors.length > 0 && (
          <div className="mt-4 flex flex-col gap-y-2">
            <Text size="small" weight="plus" className="text-ui-fg-error">
              {t("promotions.import.rowErrors")}
            </Text>
            <ul className="text-ui-fg-error list-disc pl-5">
              {rowErrors.map((error, index) => (
                <li key={index}>
                  <Text size="small">{error}</Text>
                </li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          </div>
        )}

        <Heading className="mt-6" level="h2">
          {t("promotions.import.template.title")}
        </Heading>
        <Text size="small" className="text-ui-fg-subtle">
          {t("promotions.import.template.description")}
        </Text>
        <div className="mt-4">
          <FilePreview
            filename={"promotion-import-template.csv"}
            url={templateContent}
          />
        </div>
      </RouteDrawer.Body>
      <RouteDrawer.Footer>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
          <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
            <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
              {t("actions.cancel")}
            </Button>
          </RouteDrawer.Close>
          <Button
            onClick={handleImport}
            size="small"
            disabled={!file}
            isLoading={isPending}
          >
            {t("actions.import")}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </RouteDrawer.Footer>
    </>
  )
}
```
</details></tool-use>

import {
  AdminPromotion,
  AdminPromotionRule,
  AdminRuleAttributeOption,
  AdminRuleOperatorOption,
  AdminRuleValueOption,
} from "./entities"

export interface AdminPromotionResponse {
  /**
   * The promotion's details.
   */
  promotion: AdminPromotion
}

export type AdminPromotionListResponse = PaginatedResponse<{
  /**
   * The list of promotions.
   */
  promotions: AdminPromotion[]
}>

export interface PromotionRuleResponse {
  rule: AdminPromotionRule
}

export type AdminPromotionRuleListResponse = {
  /**
   * The list of promotion rules.
   */
  rules: AdminPromotionRule[]
}

export interface RuleAttributeOptionsResponse {
  attribute: AdminRuleAttributeOption[]
}

export type AdminRuleAttributeOptionsListResponse = {
  /**
   * The list of rule attribute options.
   */
  attributes: AdminRuleAttributeOption[]
}

export interface RuleOperatorOptionsResponse {
  operator: AdminRuleOperatorOption
}

export type AdminRuleOperatorOptionsListResponse = PaginatedResponse<{
  operators: AdminRuleOperatorOption[]
}>

/**
 * @experimental
 */
export interface RuleValueOptionsResponse {
  value: AdminRuleValueOption
}

/**
 * @experimental
 */
export type AdminRuleValueOptionsListResponse = PaginatedResponse<{
  /**
   * The list of rule value options.
   */
  values: AdminRuleValueOption[]
}>

export type AdminPromotionRuleBatchResponse = BatchResponse<AdminPromotionRule>

export type AdminPromotionDeleteResponse = DeleteResponse<"promotion">

export interface AdminImportPromotionsResponse {
  /**
   * The number of promotions created by the import.
   */
  created: number
}

import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"
import { useQueryParams } from "../../use-query-params"

type UsePromotionTableQueryProps = {
  prefix?: string
  pageSize?: number
}

export const usePromotionTableQuery = ({
  prefix,
  pageSize = 20,
}: UsePromotionTableQueryProps) => {
  const queryObject = useQueryParams(
    ["offset", "q", "order", "created_at", "updated_at"],
    prefix
  )

  const { offset, q, order, created_at, updated_at } = queryObject

  const searchParams: HttpTypes.AdminGetPromotionsParams = {
    limit: pageSize,
    created_at: created_at ? JSON.parse(created_at) : undefined,
    updated_at: updated_at ? JSON.parse(updated_at) : undefined,
    offset: offset ? Number(offset) : 0,
    order,
    q,
  }

  return {
    searchParams,
    raw: queryObject,
  }
}

import { IEventBusModuleService } from "@medusajs/types"
import {
  TestEventUtils,
  medusaIntegrationTestRunner,
} from "@medusajs/test-utils"
import { CommonEvents, Modules } from "@medusajs/utils"
import fs from "fs/promises"
import { csv2json } from "json-2-csv"
import os from "os"
import path from "path"
import {
  adminHeaders,
  createAdminUser,
} from "../../../../helpers/create-admin-user"

jest.setTimeout(50000)

// The import template's header, written out from AC3 of #97 rather than read
// from the code, so a column that moves or is renamed fails this test.
const HEADER = [
  "Code",
  "Type",
  "Status",
  "Automatic",
  "Tax Inclusive",
  "Usage Limit",
  "Campaign ID",
  "Discount Type",
  "Discount Value",
  "Currency Code",
  "Target",
  "Allocation",
  "Max Quantity",
  "Buy Min Quantity",
  "Apply To Quantity",
  "Rules",
  "Target Rules",
  "Buy Rules",
]

const getCSVRows = async (filePath: string) => {
  const asLocalPath = filePath.replace("http://localhost:9000", os.tmpdir())
  const fileContent = await fs.readFile(asLocalPath, { encoding: "utf-8" })
  await fs.rm(path.dirname(asLocalPath), { recursive: true, force: true })
  return csv2json(fileContent) as Record<string, unknown>[]
}

medusaIntegrationTestRunner({
  testSuite: ({ dbConnection, api, getContainer }) => {
    let eventBus: IEventBusModuleService

    beforeEach(async () => {
      const container = getContainer()
      eventBus = container.resolve(Modules.EVENT_BUS)
      await createAdminUser(dbConnection, adminHeaders, container)

      await api.post(
        "/admin/promotions",
        {
          code: "SAVE10",
          type: "standard",
          status: "active",
          is_automatic: false,
          application_method: {
            type: "percentage",
            target_type: "items",
            allocation: "across",
            value: 10,
          },
          rules: [
            { attribute: "currency_code", operator: "eq", values: ["usd"] },
          ],
        },
        adminHeaders
      )

      await api.post(
        "/admin/promotions",
        {
          code: "BUY2GET1",
          type: "buyget",
          status: "draft",
          application_method: {
            type: "percentage",
            target_type: "items",
            allocation: "each",
            value: 100,
            max_quantity: 1,
            buy_rules_min_quantity: 2,
            apply_to_quantity: 1,
            target_rules: [
              { attribute: "product_id", operator: "in", values: ["prod_1"] },
            ],
            buy_rules: [
              { attribute: "product_id", operator: "eq", values: ["prod_2"] },
            ],
          },
        },
        adminHeaders
      )
    })

    const exportPromotions = async (query = "") => {
      const notificationCreated = TestEventUtils.waitSubscribersExecution(
        `${Modules.NOTIFICATION}.notification.${CommonEvents.CREATED}`,
        eventBus
      )

      const response = await api.post(
        `/admin/promotions/export${query}`,
        {},
        adminHeaders
      )

      expect(response.status).toEqual(202)
      expect(response.data.transaction_id).toBeTruthy()

      await notificationCreated
      const notifications = (
        await api.get("/admin/notifications", adminHeaders)
      ).data.notifications

      expect(notifications).toHaveLength(1)
      expect(notifications[0].data).toEqual(
        expect.objectContaining({
          title: "Promotion export",
          description: "Promotion export completed successfully!",
          file: expect.objectContaining({
            url: expect.stringContaining("-promotion-exports.csv"),
            mimeType: "text/csv",
          }),
        })
      )

      return getCSVRows(notifications[0].data.file.url)
    }

    describe("POST /admin/promotions/export", () => {
      it("exports every promotion using the import template's columns", async () => {
        const rows = await exportPromotions()

        expect(rows).toHaveLength(2)
        expect(Object.keys(rows[0])).toEqual(HEADER)
        expect(rows).toEqual(
          expect.arrayContaining([
            expect.objectContaining({
              Code: "SAVE10",
              Type: "standard",
              Status: "active",
              Automatic: "false",
              "Discount Type": "percentage",
              "Discount Value": "10",
              Target: "items",
              Allocation: "across",
              Rules: "currency_code:eq:usd",
            }),
            expect.objectContaining({
              Code: "BUY2GET1",
              Type: "buyget",
              Status: "draft",
              "Max Quantity": "1",
              "Buy Min Quantity": "2",
              "Apply To Quantity": "1",
              "Target Rules": "product_id:in:prod_1",
              "Buy Rules": "product_id:eq:prod_2",
            }),
          ])
        )
      })

      it("exports only the promotions matching the search", async () => {
        const rows = await exportPromotions("?q=SAVE10")

        expect(rows).toHaveLength(1)
        expect(rows[0]).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({ Code: "SAVE10" }))
      })

      it("ignores pagination and exports every matching promotion", async () => {
        const rows = await exportPromotions("?limit=1&offset=1")

        expect(rows).toHaveLength(2)
      })

      it("writes a file with only the header when nothing matches", async () => {
        const rows = await exportPromotions("?q=NOTHING_MATCHES_THIS")

        expect(rows).toHaveLength(0)
      })
    })
  },
})
EOF

import {
  FilterablePromotionProps,
  IFileModuleService,
  PromotionDTO,
} from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  Modules,
  deduplicate,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { StepResponse, createStep } from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { json2csv } from "json-2-csv"
import {
  EXPORT_COLUMNS,
  normalizePromotionForExport,
} from "../helpers/export-promotions"

/**
 * The data to export promotions.
 */
export type ExportPromotionsStepInput = {
  /**
   * The number of promotions to retrieve per batch.
   */
  batch_size?: number | string
  /**
   * The fields to select.
   */
  select: string[]
  /**
   * The filters to select which promotions to export.
   */
  filter?: FilterablePromotionProps
}

/**
 * The details of the exported file.
 */
export type ExportPromotionsStepOutput = {
  /**
   * The ID of the file.
   */
  id: string
  /**
   * The name of the file.
   */
  filename: string
}

export const exportPromotionsStepId = "export-promotions"

// Everything a row of the import template is built from. The application
// method and the three rule lists are nested, so they have to be asked for
// explicitly or the row comes back half empty.
const EXPORT_FIELDS = [
  "id",
  "code",
  "type",
  "status",
  "is_automatic",
  "is_tax_inclusive",
  "limit",
  "campaign_id",
  "application_method.type",
  "application_method.value",
  "application_method.target_type",
  "application_method.allocation",
  "application_method.currency_code",
  "application_method.max_quantity",
  "application_method.buy_rules_min_quantity",
  "application_method.apply_to_quantity",
  "application_method.target_rules.attribute",
  "application_method.target_rules.operator",
  "application_method.target_rules.values.value",
  "application_method.buy_rules.attribute",
  "application_method.buy_rules.operator",
  "application_method.buy_rules.values.value",
  "rules.attribute",
  "rules.operator",
  "rules.values.value",
]

/**
 * This step exports the promotions matching the filters to a CSV file in the
 * promotion import's format and uploads it with the File Module. It retrieves
 * the promotions in batches, so any pagination in the filters is ignored. The
 * file always has a header row, even when no promotions match.
 */
export const exportPromotionsStep = createStep(
  exportPromotionsStepId,
  async (input: ExportPromotionsStepInput, { container }) => {
    const query = container.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.QUERY)
    const fileModule = container.resolve(Modules.FILE)

    const filename = `${Date.now()}-promotion-exports.csv`
    const { writeStream, promise, fileKey } = await fileModule.getUploadStream({
      filename,
      mimeType: "text/csv",
    })

    const pageSize = !isNaN(parseInt(input?.batch_size as string))
      ? parseInt(input?.batch_size as string, 10)
      : 50

    let lastId: string | undefined
    let hasHeader = false

    const fields = deduplicate([...input.select, ...EXPORT_FIELDS])

    const filter = input.filter ?? {}

    while (true) {
      // Page with an id cursor instead of an offset, so promotions sharing a
      // created_at, or added and deleted during the export, aren't skipped or
      // repeated. The cursor goes in $and so it can't replace an id filter.
      const { data: promotions } = await query.graph({
        entity: "promotion",
        filters: lastId
          ? {
              ...filter,
              $and: [...(filter.$and ?? []), { id: { $gt: lastId } }],
            }
          : filter,
        pagination: {
          take: pageSize,
          order: { id: "ASC" },
        },
        fields,
      })

      if (promotions.length === 0) {
        break
      }

      const batchCsv = json2csv(
        promotions.map((promotion) =>
          normalizePromotionForExport(promotion as PromotionDTO)
        ),
        {
          keys: EXPORT_COLUMNS,
          prependHeader: !hasHeader,
          preventCsvInjection: true,
          emptyFieldValue: "",
        }
      )

      const ok = writeStream.write((hasHeader ? "\n" : "") + batchCsv)
      if (!ok) {
        await new Promise((resolve) => writeStream.once("drain", resolve))
      }

      hasHeader = true
      lastId = promotions[promotions.length - 1].id

      if (promotions.length < pageSize) {
        break
      }
    }

    if (!hasHeader) {
      writeStream.write(EXPORT_COLUMNS.join(","))
    }

    writeStream.end()

    await promise

    return new StepResponse(
      { id: fileKey, filename } as ExportPromotionsStepOutput,
      fileKey
    )
  },
  async (fileId, { container }) => {
    if (!fileId) {
      return
    }

    const fileModule: IFileModuleService = container.resolve(Modules.FILE)
    await fileModule.deleteFiles(fileId)
  }
)
EOF
cat > packages/core/core-flows/src/promotion/workflows/export-promotions.ts <<'EOF'
import { FilterablePromotionProps } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  WorkflowData,
  createWorkflow,
  transform,
} from "@medusajs/framework/workflows-sdk"
import { useRemoteQueryStep } from "../../common"
import { notifyOnFailureStep, sendNotificationsStep } from "../../notification"
import { exportPromotionsStep } from "../steps/export-promotions"

/**
 * The data to export promotions.
 */
export type ExportPromotionsWorkflowInput = {
  /**
   * The fields to select. These fields will be passed to
   * [Query](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/module-links/query).
   */
  select: string[]
  /**
   * The filters to select which promotions to export.
   */
  filter?: FilterablePromotionProps
}

export const exportPromotionsWorkflowId = "export-promotions"
/**
 * This workflow exports promotions matching the specified filters to a CSV
 * file in the promotion import's format. It runs in the background.
 *
 * :::note
 *
 * This workflow doesn't return the exported promotions. Instead, it sends a notification to the admin
 * users that they can download the exported promotions.
 *
 * :::
 *
 * @example
 * To export all promotions:
 *
 * ```ts
 * const { transaction } = await exportPromotionsWorkflow(container)
 * .run({
 *   input: {
 *     select: ["*"],
 *   }
 * })
 * ```
 *
 * To export promotions matching a criteria:
 *
 * ```ts
 * const { transaction } = await exportPromotionsWorkflow(container)
 * .run({
 *   input: {
 *     select: ["*"],
 *     filter: {
 *       status: "active"
 *     }
 *   }
 * })
 * ```
 *
 * @summary
 *
 * Export promotions to a CSV file.
 */
export const exportPromotionsWorkflow = createWorkflow(
  exportPromotionsWorkflowId,
  (input: WorkflowData<ExportPromotionsWorkflowInput>): WorkflowData<void> => {
    const file = exportPromotionsStep(input).config({
      async: true,
      backgroundExecution: true,
    })

    const failureNotification = transform({ input }, (data) => {
      return [
        {
          // We don't need the recipient here for now, but if we want to push feed notifications to a specific user we could add it.
          to: "",
          channel: "feed",
          template: "admin-ui",
          data: {
            title: "Promotion export",
            description: `Failed to export promotions, please try again later.`,
          },
        },
      ]
    })
    notifyOnFailureStep(failureNotification)

    const fileDetails = useRemoteQueryStep({
      fields: ["id", "url"],
      entry_point: "file",
      variables: { id: file.id },
      list: false,
    })

    const notifications = transform({ fileDetails, file }, (data) => {
      return [
        {
          // We don't need the recipient here for now, but if we want to push feed notifications to a specific user we could add it.
          to: "",
          channel: "feed",
          template: "admin-ui",
          data: {
            title: "Promotion export",
            description: "Promotion export completed successfully!",
            file: {
              filename: data.file.filename,
              url: data.fileDetails.url,
              mimeType: "text/csv",
            },
          },
        },
      ]
    })

    sendNotificationsStep(notifications)
  }
)

import { exportPromotionsWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import { FilterablePromotionProps, HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<{}, HttpTypes.AdminGetPromotionsParams>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminExportPromotionsResponse>
) => {
  const selectFields = req.queryConfig.fields ?? []
  // filterableFields doesn't include limit and offset, so every promotion
  // matching the filters is exported, not only the current page.
  const input = {
    select: selectFields,
    filter: req.filterableFields as FilterablePromotionProps,
  }

  const { transaction } = await exportPromotionsWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input,
  })

  res.status(202).json({ transaction_id: transaction.transactionId })
}

import { Button, Heading, Text, toast } from "@medusajs/ui"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { RouteDrawer, useRouteModal } from "../../../components/modals"
import { useExportPromotions } from "../../../hooks/api/promotions"
import { usePromotionTableQuery } from "../../../hooks/table/query/use-promotion-table-query"

export const PromotionExport = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <RouteDrawer>
      <RouteDrawer.Header>
        <RouteDrawer.Title asChild>
          <Heading>{t("promotions.export.header")}</Heading>
        </RouteDrawer.Title>
        <RouteDrawer.Description className="sr-only">
          {t("promotions.export.description")}
        </RouteDrawer.Description>
      </RouteDrawer.Header>
      <PromotionExportContent />
    </RouteDrawer>
  )
}

const PromotionExportContent = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  // The list's Export link forwards its query string, so this reads the same
  // filters and search that are applied to the promotion list.
  const { searchParams } = usePromotionTableQuery({})

  const { mutateAsync } = useExportPromotions(searchParams)
  const { handleSuccess } = useRouteModal()

  const handleExportRequest = async () => {
    await mutateAsync(searchParams, {
      onSuccess: () => {
        // The export runs in a background workflow, so the response only
        // contains its transaction ID. The CSV's download URL arrives later as
        // a notification.
        toast.info(t("promotions.export.success.title"), {
          description: t("promotions.export.success.description"),
        })
        handleSuccess()
      },
      onError: (err) => {
        toast.error(err.message)
      },
    })
  }

  return (
    <>
      <RouteDrawer.Body>
        <Text size="small" className="text-ui-fg-subtle">
          {t("promotions.export.description")}
        </Text>
      </RouteDrawer.Body>
      <RouteDrawer.Footer>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
          <RouteDrawer.Close asChild>
            <Button size="small" variant="secondary">
              {t("actions.cancel")}
            </Button>
          </RouteDrawer.Close>
          <Button onClick={handleExportRequest} size="small">
            {t("actions.export")}
          </Button>
        </div>
      </RouteDrawer.Footer>
    </>
  )
}

3 of 4 pass. The failure is my test's fault, not the code's: `csv2json` coerces `"false"` to boolean and `"10"` to number when reading back, so the parsed row never shows the strings the converter wrote.

That's worth fixing properly rather than matching the coerced values, since AC5 is specifically about the text written to the file:

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-11-18 23:02:56Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>

```bash
cd ~/medusa && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("integration-tests/http/__tests__/promotions/admin/promotion-export.spec.ts")
t = p.read_text()

old_helper = '''const getCSVRows = async (filePath: string) => {
  const asLocalPath = filePath.replace("http://localhost:9000", os.tmpdir())
  const fileContent = await fs.readFile(asLocalPath, { encoding: "utf-8" })
  await fs.rm(path.dirname(asLocalPath), { recursive: true, force: true })
  return csv2json(fileContent) as Record<string, unknown>[]
}'''
new_helper = '''// csv2json coerces "false" to a boolean and "10" to a number, so the parsed
// rows can't show how a value was written. The raw text is kept alongside them
// for the assertions about the file's own formatting.
const readCSV = async (filePath: string) => {
  const asLocalPath = filePath.replace("http://localhost:9000", os.tmpdir())
  const text = await fs.readFile(asLocalPath, { encoding: "utf-8" })
  await fs.rm(path.dirname(asLocalPath), { recursive: true, force: true })
  return { text, rows: csv2json(text) as Record<string, unknown>[] }
}

const lineFor = (text: string, code: string) =>
  text.split("\\n").find((line) => line.startsWith(`${code},`))'''
assert t.count(old_helper) == 1
t = t.replace(old_helper, new_helper)

t = t.replace(
    "      return getCSVRows(notifications[0].data.file.url)",
    "      return readCSV(notifications[0].data.file.url)",
)

              "Apply To Quantity": "1",
              "Target Rules": "product_id:in:prod_1",
              "Buy Rules": "product_id:eq:prod_2",
            }),
          ])
        )
      })'''
new_test = '''      it("exports every promotion using the import template's columns", async () => {
        const { text, rows } = await exportPromotions()

        expect(rows).toHaveLength(2)
        expect(text.split("\\n")[0]).toEqual(HEADER.join(","))
        expect(Object.keys(rows[0])).toEqual(HEADER)

      it("writes each promotion as one row in the import's format", async () => {

Closes #97

What: Adds a promotion CSV export. The Promotions list has an Export action next to Import. It opens a drawer, and confirming starts a background export of every promotion matching the list's current filters and search. The file uses the promotion import's columns, so an exported file can be imported again.

Why: Promotions could be imported but not exported, so there was no way to review them in a spreadsheet, keep a backup, or move them to another store. My spec review and the answers to the issue's open questions are on #97.

How: It follows the customer export file for file: a step that pages through promotions with an id cursor and streams the CSV to the File Module, a workflow that runs the step in the background and sends a feed notification on success or failure, `POST /admin/promotions/export` returning 202 with a transaction ID, an SDK method, and the Export action on the list.

The one deliberate difference is that the row conversion stays in `export-promotions.ts`, where the first commits on this branch put it, instead of living inside the step as the customer version does. The step imports `normalizePromotionForExport` and `EXPORT_COLUMNS` from there. The columns come from the import's own `COLUMNS` map rather than a second copy of the list, so the two can't drift when a column is added later.

Rules go out in the import's `attribute:operator:value1|value2` form, booleans as `true` and `false`, and anything the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell. A rule with no readable values is left out rather than written in a form the import would reject. The Export link carries the list's query string, which is how the drawer reads the same filters the list is showing.

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC1: the promotions list has an Export action next to Import | `promotion-list-table.spec.tsx > links to the promotion export from the list header` | unit | AC |
| AC2: the export covers every promotion matching the list's filters and search, not only the current page | `promotion-list-table.spec.tsx > forwards the list's filters and search to the export`; `promotion-export.spec.tsx > sends the list's current filters with the export request`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > exports only the promotions matching the search`; `> ignores pagination and exports every matching promotion` | unit, integration | AC |
| AC3: same column headers, in the same order, as the import template | `export-promotions.spec.ts > uses the import template's columns in the template's order`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > exports every promotion using the import template's columns` | unit, integration | AC. The header is a literal in both tests, written from the list in AC3, not read from the code |
| AC4: rules use `attribute:operator:value`, values joined by `\|`, rules by `;` | `export-promotions.spec.ts > joins a rule's values with `\|` and separate rules with `;``; `> writes the buyget quantities and both rule columns`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > writes each promotion as one row in the import's format` | unit, integration | AC. The expected string is AC4's own worked example |
| AC5: empty fields are empty cells, booleans are `true`/`false` | `export-promotions.spec.ts > flattens a promotion and its application method into one row`; `> leaves a field the promotion doesn't have as an empty cell`; `> writes a limit of 0 and a value of 0 rather than treating them as unset`; `promotion-export.spec.ts > writes each promotion as one row in the import's format` | unit, integration | AC. The integration test asserts the file's raw text, because the CSV reader coerces `false` and `10` back to a boolean and a number |
| AC6: importing an exported file recreates the promotion, checked with the existing import parser | `export-promotions.spec.ts > recreates a standard promotion with the same settings and rules`; `> recreates a buyget promotion with its quantities and both rule sets`; `> exports every promotion in the file, one row each` | unit | AC. The expected `CreatePromotionDTO` is written out by hand from the source promotion, not captured from a run |
| AC7: the export runs in the background, the route returns 202 with a `transaction_id`, and a notification carries the download link | `promotion-export.spec.ts`, in the `exportPromotions` helper every test goes through: it asserts the 202, the transaction ID, and the feed notification with the CSV's URL and `text/csv` type | integration | AC |
| AC8: unit tests for the conversion including rule formatting and the round trip, an HTTP integration test for the route and its filters, and a dashboard test for the Export action | All three: `export-promotions.spec.ts` (16 tests), `promotion-export.spec.ts` (5 tests), `promotion-export.spec.tsx` and `promotion-list-table.spec.tsx` (7 tests) | unit, integration | AC |

Not tested automatically, and why: nothing is manual-only. One gap worth naming though: I have not clicked the Export action in a running dashboard, so AC1 and AC2 are covered at the component level by the href and the request the drawer sends, not end to end in a browser.

AI-written tests: the step, workflow, route, drawer and all the tests on this branch were drafted with Claude Code. No expected value was copied from the output of code this PR adds, with one deliberate exception noted under Tech Debt. The headers and rule strings come from AC3 and AC4, the round trip's expected result is written out from the source promotion by hand, and the two exact CSV rows in the integration test were written from AC3's column order plus AC4 and AC5's formatting rules before the test was run; both matched on the first run.

Two things I had to correct. My first integration assertions expected `Automatic` to be the string `"false"` and `Discount Value` the string `"10"`, and the test failed: `csv2json` coerces those back to a boolean and a number when it reads the file, so a parsed row can never show how a value was written. The test now asserts the raw file text for AC5, which is what the criterion is actually about. Separately, the typecheck caught `useExportPromotions` taking a `query` argument it never used; it now passes it to the SDK the way `useExportCustomers` does.

CI doesn't run on PRs here, so these runs stand in for it.

## Tech Debt

Introduced: a rule value containing `;`, `|` or `:` exports fine but reads back as a different rule, because the import splits on those. In practice these values are IDs and currency codes. There's a test pinning the behavior so it's documented rather than discovered, and that is the one expected value taken from existing code rather than an AC, since it records what the import parser does today. The reasoning is in my comment on #97, and fixing it means an escaping scheme on both sides, which is its own issue.

Introduced: `useExportPromotions` takes the filters as a hook argument and ignores the payload passed to `mutateAsync`, which is how `useExportCustomers` works. The drawer passes the same value to both, so it behaves correctly, but the mutation's payload type is misleading.

Encountered: `en.json` has `"duplicate": "Duplicate"` twice in the `actions` block, at lines 120 and 147. JSON parsers keep the last one, so nothing is broken, but a round trip through a JSON parser silently drops one. I hit that while adding the export keys and switched to a text insert to leave it alone. It predates this branch.

Encountered: the export is tied to the import's template by design, so a promotion field with no column can't be exported. Usage counts, campaign details and campaign budgets are the ones that come up, and the issue lists them as out of scope.

Encountered: this branch is 16 commits behind develop, including the bundles API and the low-stock dashboard. Nothing it touches overlaps, and the suites above pass, but it should take a merge from develop before it goes in.

    paths:
      - packages/admin/dashboard/src/i18n/translations/**

jobs:
  i18n-validation-admin-dashboard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "yarn"

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: packages/admin/dashboard
        run: yarn install

      - name: Validate i18n translations
        working-directory: packages/admin/dashboard
        run: |
          git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A origin/develop HEAD -- src/i18n/translations > i18n_added_files.txt

          cat i18n_added_files.txt

          while read -r file; do
            # Get the base name of the file
            filename=$(basename "$file")

            # Skip those items
            if [ "$filename" = "\$schema.json" ] || [ "$filename" = "index.ts" ] || [ -d "$file" ]; then
              continue
            fi

            # Run validation on the file
            yarn i18n:validate "$filename"
          done < i18n_added_files.txt
```

```text
### D6 - Mutation Testing (15 pts, individual) - NEW

**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (**mutants**), such as
flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test
fails, the mutant is **killed**. If all tests pass, the mutant **survived**: your tests did not
notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

**What to do.** For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests
(**CSCI 535: two such issues**; your small issue may be one of them):

1. Run a mutation testing tool **on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue**. Do not
   run it on the whole project.
2. Using the tool's report, **analyze every surviving mutant**: is it **equivalent** (it behaves
   exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a **gap** in your
   tests? If there are more than 10 survivors, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines
   your PR added or changed.
3. **Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant** that revealed a gap.
   Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no survivor reveals a gap (all killed or equivalent),
   say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
4. Answer the questions in the template.

**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (**StrykerJS: add `"json"` to
`reporters`**). Commit the report from the first run and the re-run as
`docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json`. The mutation
scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in
the "after" report.

**A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.**

| Stack | Tool |
|---|---|
| **TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)** | **StrykerJS with the Jest runner** |
| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| Go | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

**Note for us:** Medusa is mixed. Backend packages use **Jest**, the dashboard uses **Vitest**.
Pick the runner that matches the files the PR changed.

**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services,
choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits
the configuration used. **You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to)**, as long as you
run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

**Common problems to watch for:**
- **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any
  selected test fails, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where the baseline
  run helps). *Relevant to us: see HANDOFF section 3 and issue #98.*
- **Tests run against built code.** If tests run against compiled output (a `dist` folder) instead
  of the source, mutants in the source are never seen. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing,
  or choose tests that run on source. *Relevant to us: the integration tests load `dist`.*
- **Tests need services.** Some suites need a database or another service running. Start them first.
- **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run, make sure the tests that cover the mutated
  files are included. Otherwise mutants some test would catch are reported as survived or not
  covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
- **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by the PR keeps run time manageable.

**If you are blocked:** ask teammates first, someone may have a working setup. Still stuck, tell the
TA **as early as possible**, with the errors and the AI log of what you tried. The TA may approve
running the tool on a different issue or part of the code. **Problems reported at the end of the
sprint will not excuse a missing D6.**

**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-angrapsas.md`, using this template:

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>

**PR(s):** #...
**Tool:** ...
**Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]
**Command:** `...`
**Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%

## Surviving mutants

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [link] · Test: [file > test name] · Kills: [mutant location]

## Questions

1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the
   requirements? Explain.
3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and
   what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."
```

**Rubric:**

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| Tool run on the files changed by the PR; configuration, command, results and reports committed | 4 |
| Surviving mutants analyzed correctly (equivalent vs test gap, with explanation) | 4 |
| At least one new or strengthened test kills a surviving mutant; re-run confirms it | 4 |
| Answers to the questions show understanding, not just description | 3 |

**CSCI 535: the D6 score is the average of the two submissions.**

// StrykerJS config for D6 mutation testing in @medusajs/core-flows.
//
// Adapted from njpiombino's setup for issue #62
// (packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json on develop) and from
// lefecko's root stryker.config.mjs for issue #112. Credit to both; see
// docs/sprint3/mutation/97-angrapsas.md.
//
// Stryker is NOT a committed dependency, so package.json and yarn.lock stay
// untouched. `npm install --no-save` cannot be used in this repo (npm fails to
// re-resolve the yarn-managed tree: a pre-existing rollup/vite peer conflict),
// so install it outside the repo and call its binary by path:
//
//   mkdir -p /tmp/stryker && cd /tmp/stryker
//   npm init -y && npm install @stryker-mutator/core@10 @stryker-mutator/jest-runner@10
//
// Usage: run from THIS directory so Jest picks up this package's jest.config.js.
//
//   STRYKER_MUTATE="src/promotion/helpers/export-promotions.ts" \
//   STRYKER_TEST="src/promotion/helpers/__tests__/export-promotions.spec.ts" \
//   STRYKER_JSON_REPORT="../../../docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/97-angrapsas-before.json" \
//   node /tmp/stryker/node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.config.mjs
//
// Retargeting to another file in this package is two env vars and no edit to
// this file. Retargeting to a different Jest package is a copy of this file
// into that package (the paths below are all relative to the package).

const repoRoot = "../../.."

/** @type {import("@stryker-mutator/api/core").PartialStrykerOptions} */
export default {
  testRunner: "jest",

  jest: {
    // Use this package's jest.config.js, which transforms src/ with @swc/jest.
    // These tests run on SOURCE, not on dist/, so no build step is needed
    // before testing (unlike the inventory module tests njpiombino mutated).
    configFile: "jest.config.js",
    // Run only the spec(s) that cover the mutated file. Checked by grep that
    // nothing else imports it, so this cannot hide a killer test.
    config: {
      testMatch: [
        `<rootDir>/${process.env.STRYKER_TEST ?? "src/**/*.spec.ts"}`,
      ],
    },
    // Stryker's own test filtering is used instead of Jest's
    // --findRelatedTests, which resolves against dist/ here.
    enableFindRelatedTests: false,
  },

  // The file(s) the PR changed. Never the whole package.
  mutate: [process.env.STRYKER_MUTATE ?? "src/**/*.ts"],

  // "perTest" only runs the tests that touch each mutant. Verified against a
  // full `coverageAnalysis: "all"` run on this target: identical results, so
  // it is not under-reporting coverage here.
  coverageAnalysis: "perTest",

  // Mutants run in the package itself, not in a copied sandbox: package jest
  // configs use a relative require("../../../define_jest_config"), which breaks
  // from a sandbox two directories deeper. Stryker restores the sources when
  // the run ends; if a run is killed midway, `git checkout -- .` cleans up.
  inPlace: true,

  // Scratch dir at the repo root, so Jest does not discover Stryker's backup
  // copy of this package's tests and run everything twice.
  tempDirName: `${repoRoot}/.stryker-tmp`,

  timeoutMS: 60000,
}

# Mutation testing: Issue #97 -- Export promotions to CSV

**PR(s):** #108
**Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Jest runner (`@stryker-mutator/core`, `@stryker-mutator/jest-runner`)
**Config:** [packages/core/core-flows/stryker.config.mjs](../../../packages/core/core-flows/stryker.config.mjs), adapted from njpiombino's setup for #62 ([packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/blob/develop/packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json)) and lefecko's root [stryker.config.mjs](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa/blob/develop/stryker.config.mjs) for #112. Credit to both; what I changed and why is under Setup below. Those two links point at `develop`, because this branch is behind it and does not contain either file yet.
**Command:**

```

STRYKER_MUTATE="src/promotion/helpers/export-promotions.ts" \
STRYKER_TEST="src/promotion/helpers/__tests__/export-promotions.spec.ts" \
STRYKER_JSON_REPORT="../../../docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/97-angrapsas-before.json" \
node /tmp/stryker/node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.config.mjs
```

(`-after.json` for the re-run; nothing else changes.)
